<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">PART I</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: left">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Item 1&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Business</font></font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">BFS Bancorp, MHC</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">BFS Bancorp, MHC is the federally chartered mutual holding company parent of Brooklyn Federal Bancorp, Inc.&#160;&#160;The only business that BFS Bancorp, MHC has engaged in is the majority ownership of Brooklyn Federal Bancorp, Inc.&#160;&#160;BFS Bancorp, MHC was formed upon completion of Brooklyn Federal Savings Bank&#8217;s reorganization
into the mutual holding company structure.&#160;&#160;So long as BFS Bancorp, MHC exists, it will own a majority of the voting stock of Brooklyn Federal Bancorp, Inc.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Brooklyn Federal Bancorp, Inc.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Brooklyn Federal Bancorp, Inc. (the &#8220;Company&#8221;) was formed to serve as the stock holding company for Brooklyn Federal Savings Bank (the &#8220;Bank&#8221;) as part of the Bank&#8217;s reorganization into the mutual holding company structure.&#160;&#160;For further discussion of the Company&#8217;s formation and operations, see
the Company&#8217;s Registration Statement on Form&#160;S-1, as amended, declared effective by the Securities and Exchange Commission (the &#8220;SEC&#8221;) on February&#160;11, 2005 (File Number 333-121580).&#160;&#160;The Company completed its initial public offering on April 5, 2005.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Company issued 9,257,500 shares to BFS Bancorp, MHC, resulting in a total of 13,225,000 shares issued and outstanding after completion of the reorganization.&#160;&#160;At September 30, 2009, there were 12,890,754 total shares outstanding resulting in a 71.8% ownership by BFS Bancorp, MHC.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Brooklyn Federal Savings Bank</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Bank is a federally chartered savings bank headquartered in Brooklyn, New York.&#160;&#160;The Bank was originally founded in 1887.&#160;&#160;We conduct our business from our main office and four branch offices.&#160;&#160;The Bank opened its fifth full-service office in Commack, Suffolk County, New York on April 30, 2008.&#160;&#160;All
of our offices are located in New York.&#160;&#160;The telephone number at our main office is (718) 855-8500.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At September 30, 2009, we had total assets of $521.4 million, total deposits of $402.1 million and stockholders&#8217; equity of $81.9 million.&#160;&#160;Our net income for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2009 was $1.3 million.&#160;&#160;Our principal business activity is the origination of mortgage loans secured by one- to four-family
residential real estate, multi-family real estate, commercial real estate, construction loans, land loans and, to a limited extent, a variety of consumer loans and home equity loans.&#160;&#160;The Bank offers a variety of deposit accounts, including checking, savings and certificates of deposit, and it emphasizes personal and efficient service for its customers.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our website address is www.brooklynbank.com.&#160;&#160;Information on our website should not be considered a part of this document.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Competition</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We face intense competition within our market area both in making loans and attracting deposits.&#160;&#160;The New York City metropolitan area has a high concentration of financial institutions including large money center and regional banks, community banks and credit unions.&#160;&#160;Some of our competitors offer products and services
that we currently do not offer, such as trust services and private banking.&#160;&#160;As of June 30, 2009, our market share of deposits represented 0.57%, 0.15% and 0.22% of deposits in each of Kings, Nassau and Suffolk Counties, New York, respectively.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our competition for loans and deposits comes principally from commercial banks, savings institutions, mortgage banking firms and credit unions.&#160;&#160;We face additional competition for deposits from short-term money market funds, brokerage firms, mutual funds and insurance companies.&#160;&#160;Our primary focus is to develop and
build profitable customer relationships across all lines of business while maintaining our role as a community bank.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">&#160;</div></div>
<div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; WIDTH: 100%">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">1</font></div>
<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
<hr style="COLOR: gainsboro" align="left" noshade size="2" width="100%"></div></div>
<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right">&#160;</div></div></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Market Area</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We are part of the diverse economy of the New York City metropolitan area.&#160;&#160;Brooklyn (Kings County) is an urban market area while Nassau and Suffolk Counties are suburban.&#160;&#160;Our market area has a stable population and household base.&#160;&#160;In 2008, the median household income for Kings, Nassau, and Suffolk Counties
was $43,172, $94,856 and $85,091, respectively.&#160;&#160;Our primary lending area is concentrated in Brooklyn and Nassau and Suffolk Counties, New York, although we originate loans in all five boroughs of New York City as well as Westchester County, New York.&#160;&#160;One- to four-family residential real estate in our market area is characterized by a large number of attached and semi-detached houses, including a number of two- and three-family homes and cooperative apartments.&#160;&#160;Most of our deposit
customers are residents of the greater New York metropolitan area.&#160;&#160;Our customer base consists primarily of middle-income households, and to a lesser extent, low- to moderate-income households.&#160;&#160;The median household income for Brooklyn is below the national and New York state median household incomes.&#160;&#160;In addition, the unemployment rate in Kings County is higher than in the surrounding suburbs.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Lending Activities</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Although historically, our principal lending activity was the origination of first mortgage loans for the purchase or refinancing of one- to four-family residential real property, our focus has been increasingly towards the origination of multi-family, commercial real estate, construction and land loans in an effort to increase interest
income.&#160;&#160;These loans have increased from 72.9% of our total loans receivable at September 30, 2005 to 82.0% of our total loans receivable at September 30, 2009.&#160;&#160;Commercial real estate loans totaled $143.2 million, or 33.2% of our total loans receivable at September 30, 2009.&#160;&#160;One- to four-family residential real estate mortgage loans represented $77.1 million, or 17.9%, of our loans receivable at September 30, 2009.&#160;&#160;Multi-family real estate loans totaled $92.4 million,
or 21.4% of the total loans receivable at September 30, 2009.&#160;&#160;Construction loans totaled $73.3 million, or 17.0% and land loans totaled $45.0 million, or 10.4% of the total loans receivable at September 30, 2009.&#160;&#160;At September 30, 2009, we had no loans in loans held-for-sale compared to $8.6 million in loans held-for-sale at September 30, 2005.&#160;&#160;On a limited basis, we originate consumer loans.&#160;&#160;We sell most of our longer-term residential loans to the Federal Home Loan
Bank of New York and other investors, on a servicing-retained basis. We syndicate and sell participation interests in portions of our multi-family, commercial real estate and construction loans because of our legal lending limits and our internal portfolio management guidelines.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">

during fiscal year 2009, the Company transferred $200.5 million in loans held-for-sale to the loans receivable portfolio.&#160;&#160;These loan transfers occurred throughout the fiscal year ended September 30, 2009 and are reflected in the loans receivable portfolio balances as of September 30, 2009.&#160;&#160;As of September 30, 2009, the Company held no loans in the loans held-for-sale portfolio.</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Loan Originations, Sales and Repayments</font>.&#160;&#160;Historically, we have originated one- to four-family&#160;&#160;mortgage loans pursuant to underwriting standards that generally conform
to government-sponsored agency guidelines.&#160;&#160;Loan origination activities are primarily concentrated in New York, Kings, Nassau and Suffolk Counties, New York.&#160;&#160;New loans are generated primarily from walk-in customers, customer referrals, a network of mortgage brokers, and other parties with whom we do business, and from the efforts of employees and advertising.&#160;&#160;Loan applications are underwritten and processed at our main office in Brooklyn, New York.&#160;&#160;We syndicate and sell
participation interests in portions of our multi-family, commercial real estate and construction loans because of our legal lending limits and our internal portfolio management guidelines.&#160;&#160;We generally sell longer-term, fixed rate mortgage loans and generally retain in our portfolio the majority of our adjustable rate and shorter-term, fixed rate mortgage loans.</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In loan participation transactions, we originate and fund the full loan amount and subsequently identify other lending institutions who purchase participation interests in the loan.&#160;&#160;For purposes of the table above, originations of these loans are included within our total origination activity and the subsequent sales are shown
as deductions.&#160;&#160;Participations differ from loan syndication transactions that are not transfers of financial assets for financial reporting purposes.&#160;&#160;As the manager of a loan syndication, prior to closing the loan, we identify other lenders who agree to fund portions of the total loan at closing.&#160;&#160;We record our share of the loan syndication as a loans receivable and therefore have included in the table above only those amounts within total loan originations in the above table.&#160;&#160;The
amounts funded by other syndication lenders, which are not reflected as loan originations and sales in our consolidated financial statements and therefore are excluded from the table, totaled $54.9 million, $129.7 million and $76.8 million for syndications completed during the years ended September 30, 2009, 2008 and 2007, respectively.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">One- to Four-Family Residential Loans.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font>Historically,
our primary lending activity has consisted of the origination of one- to four-family residential mortgage loans secured primarily by properties located in Kings, Nassau and Suffolk Counties, New York.&#160;&#160;At September 30, 2009, approximately $77.1 million, or 17.9% of our loans receivable consisted of one- to four-family residential loans.&#160;&#160;Our originations of one- to four-family loans decreased by $4.8 million compared to 2008.&#160;&#160;Generally, one- to four-family residential mortgage loans
are originated in amounts up to 80% of the lesser of the appraised value or purchase price of the property.&#160;&#160;Private mortgage insurance is required on loans with a loan-to-value ratio in excess of 80%.&#160;&#160;We originate and sell in the secondary market one- to four-family residential mortgage loans in excess of the 80% loan-to-value ratio without private mortgage insurance.&#160;&#160;Fixed-rate loans are originated for terms of 10, 15, 20, 25 and 30 years.&#160;&#160;At September 30, 2009, our
largest loan secured by one- to four-family real estate had a principal balance of approximately $2.6 million and our second largest loan secured by one- to four-family real estate had a principal balance of approximately $1.8 million.&#160;&#160;The loans were secured by a two-family and a one-family residence, respectively.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We also offer adjustable rate mortgage loans with one and three-year adjustment periods based on changes in a designated U.S. Treasury index and prime rate.&#160;&#160;We originated $9.3 million of adjustable rate one- to four-family residential loans during the year ended September 30, 2009 and $2.4 million during the year ended September
30, 2008.&#160;&#160;Our adjustable rate mortgage loans provide for maximum rate adjustments of 200<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font>basis points per adjustment, with a lifetime maximum adjustment of 600 basis points.&#160;&#160;We currently do not offer adjustable rate mortgage loans with interest rates that adjust below the initial interest rate or adjustable rate mortgage loans with terms that provide the borrower options with regard
to the amount or timing of periodic payments.&#160;&#160;Our adjustable rate mortgage loans amortize over terms of up to 30 years.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">&#160;</div></div>
<div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; WIDTH: 100%">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">7</font></div>
<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
<hr style="COLOR: gainsboro" align="left" noshade size="2" width="100%"></div></div>
<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right">&#160;</div></div></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Adjustable rate mortgage loans decrease the risk associated with changes in market interest rates by periodically repricing, but involve other risks because, as interest rates increase, the interest payments on the loan increase, thus increasing the potential for default by the borrower.&#160;&#160;At the same time, the marketability of
the underlying collateral may be adversely affected by higher interest rates.&#160;&#160;Upward adjustment of the contractual interest rate is also limited by the maximum periodic and lifetime interest rate adjustments permitted by our loan documents, and therefore, is potentially limited in effectiveness during periods of extended or rapidly rising interest rates.&#160;&#160;At September 30, 2009, $8.8 million, or 11.4%, of our one- to four-family residential loans had adjustable rates of interest.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">All one- to four-family residential mortgage loans that we originate include &#8220;due-on-sale&#8221; clauses, which give us the right to declare a loan immediately due and payable in the event that, among other things, the borrower sells or otherwise disposes of the real property subject to the mortgage and the loan is not repaid.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Regulations limit the amount that a savings association may lend relative to the appraised value of the real estate securing the loan, as determined by an appraisal of the property at the time the loan is originated.&#160;&#160;For all loans, we utilize outside independent appraisers approved by our board of directors.&#160;&#160;All borrowers
are required to obtain title insurance, except for equity loans with balances under $50,000.&#160;&#160;We also require fire and casualty insurance and, where circumstances warrant, flood insurance.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Multi-Family Real Estate Loans.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font>Loans secured
by multi-family real estate totaled approximately $92.4 million, or 21.4% of the total loans receivable at September 30, 2009.&#160;&#160;Multi-family real estate loans generally are secured by rental properties (including multi-family apartment buildings).&#160;&#160;Substantially all multi-family real estate loans are secured by properties located within our lending area.&#160;&#160;At September 30, 2009, we had 63 multi-family real estate loans with an average principal balance of $1.47 million.&#160;&#160;At
September 30, 2009, our largest multi-family real estate loan balance was $10.2 million.&#160;&#160;Multi-family real estate loans generally are offered with fixed interest rates.&#160;&#160;Multi-family real estate loans also generally are originated for terms ranging from one year to 15 years with the majority of these loans being originated for shorter terms within this range. <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Bank agreed with the OTS that, other than contractual
commitments entered into prior to December 3, 2009, the Bank will not originate any multi-family loans without prior OTS approval.</font></font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We consider a number of factors in originating multi-family real estate loans.&#160;&#160;We evaluate the qualifications and financial condition of the borrower (including credit history), profitability and expertise, as well as the value and condition of the mortgaged property securing the loan.&#160;&#160;When evaluating the qualifications
of a borrower, we consider the financial resources of the borrower, the borrower&#8217;s experience in owning or managing similar property and the borrower&#8217;s payment history with us and other financial institutions.&#160;&#160;In evaluating the property securing the loan, the factors we consider include the net operating income of the mortgaged property before debt service and depreciation, the ratio of the loan amount to the appraised value of the mortgaged property and the debt service coverage ratio
(the ratio of net operating income to debt service) to ensure that it is at least 120% of the monthly debt service.&#160;&#160;Multi-family real estate loans are originated in amounts up to 75% of the appraised value of the mortgaged property securing the loan.&#160;&#160;All multi-family loans are appraised by outside independent appraisers approved by our board of directors.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Loans secured by multi-family real estate generally involve a greater degree of credit risk than one- to four-family residential mortgage loans and carry larger loan balances.&#160;&#160;This increased credit risk is a result of several factors, including the concentration of principal in a limited number of loans and borrowers, the effects
of general economic conditions on income producing properties, and the increased difficulty of evaluating and monitoring these types of loans.&#160;&#160;Furthermore, the repayment of loans secured by multi-family real estate typically depends upon the successful operation of the real estate property securing the loan.&#160;&#160;If the cash flow from the project is reduced, the borrower&#8217;s ability to repay the loan may be impaired.&#160;&#160;All borrowers are required to obtain title insurance.&#160;&#160;We
also require fire and casualty insurance and, where circumstances warrant, flood insurance.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">&#160;</div></div>
<div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; WIDTH: 100%">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">8</font></div>
<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
<hr style="COLOR: gainsboro" align="left" noshade size="2" width="100%"></div></div>
<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right">&#160;</div></div></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Commercial Real Estate Loans.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font>At September 30,
2009, $143.2 million, or 33.2% of our total loans receivable, consisted of commercial real estate loans.&#160;&#160;Commercial real estate loans are secured by office buildings, mixed-use properties and other commercial properties. We generally originate fixed-rate commercial real estate loans with an initial term ranging from one to five years and a repricing option, and a maximum term of up to 20 years.&#160;&#160;The majority of commercial real estate loans originated have shorter terms within this range.&#160;&#160;The
maximum loan-to-value ratio of our commercial real estate loans is 75%.&#160;&#160;At September 30, 2009, we had 88 commercial real estate loans with an average outstanding balance of $1.6 million.&#160;&#160;At September 30, 2009, our largest commercial real estate loan balance was $8.8 million. <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Bank agreed with the OTS that, other than contractual commitments entered into prior to December 3, 2009, the Bank will not originate any
commercial real estate loans without prior OTS approval.</font></font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We consider a number of factors in originating commercial real estate loans.&#160;&#160;We evaluate the qualifications and financial condition of the borrower, including credit history, profitability and expertise, as well as the value and condition of the mortgaged property securing the loan.&#160;&#160;When evaluating the qualifications
of the borrower, we consider the financial resources of the borrower, the borrower&#8217;s experience in owning or managing similar property and the borrower&#8217;s payment history with us and other financial institutions.&#160;&#160;In evaluating the property securing the loan, the factors we consider include the net operating income of the mortgaged property before debt service and depreciation, the ratio of the loan amount to the appraised value of the mortgaged property and the debt service coverage ratio
(the ratio of net operating income to debt service) to ensure that it is at least 120% of the monthly debt service.&#160;&#160;All commercial real estate loans are appraised by outside independent appraisers approved by our board of directors.&#160;&#160;Personal guarantees are obtained from commercial real estate borrowers although we will consider waiving this requirement based upon the loan-to-value ratio of the proposed loan.&#160;&#160;All borrowers are required to obtain title insurance.&#160;&#160;We also
require fire and casualty insurance and, where circumstances warrant, flood insurance.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Loans secured by commercial real estate generally are larger than one- to four-family residential loans and involve greater credit risk.&#160;&#160;Commercial real estate loans often involve large loan balances to single borrowers or groups of related borrowers.&#160;&#160;Repayment of these loans depends to a large degree on the results
of operations and management of the properties securing the loans or the businesses conducted on this property, and may be affected to a greater extent by adverse conditions in the real estate market or the economy in general.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, the nature of these loans makes them more difficult for management to monitor and evaluate.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Construction Loans</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">.&#160;&#160;</font>At September 30, 2009,
$73.3 million, or 17.0%, of our total loans receivable consisted of construction loans.&#160;&#160;Most of our construction loans are for the construction of multi-family and mixed-use properties.&#160;&#160;The majority of our construction loans are referred by mortgage brokers who make the initial contact with the potential borrower and forward to us additional loan information that we review to determine whether the applicant satisfies our underwriting criteria.&#160;&#160;If the loan information meets our
criteria, we issue a letter of intent listing the terms and conditions of any potential loan.&#160;&#160;If the potential borrower agrees to these terms and conditions, we will continue our standard underwriting practice.&#160;&#160;We offer primarily adjustable rate residential construction loans.&#160;&#160;Construction loans are generally structured with an option for permanent mortgage financing once the construction is completed.&#160;&#160;Construction loans generally have a two-year term and are generally
repaid from the sale of units or refinancing upon completion.&#160;&#160;These loans generally have interest rates that adjust daily with prime and generally will not have an interest rate that adjusts below the initial interest rate.&#160;&#160;Construction loans require only the payment of interest during the construction period.&#160;&#160;Construction loans will generally be made in amounts of up to 75% of the appraised value of the completed property, or the actual cost of the improvements.&#160;&#160;Funds
are disbursed based on our inspections in accordance with a schedule reflecting the completion of portions of the project.&#160;&#160;&#160;At September 30, 2009, our largest construction loan balance was $5.1 million. <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Bank agreed with the OTS that, other than contractual commitments entered into prior to December 3, 2009, the Bank will not originate any construction loans without prior OTS approval.</font></font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Construction loans generally involve a greater degree of credit risk than one- to four-family residential mortgage loans.&#160;&#160;The risk of loss on a construction loan depends upon the accuracy of the initial estimate of the value of the property at completion of construction compared to the estimated cost of construction as well
as the ability to complete construction on a timely basis, and the ability to sell or refinance the property.&#160;&#160;For all loans, we utilize outside independent appraisers approved by our board of directors.&#160;&#160;All borrowers are required to obtain title insurance.&#160;&#160;We also require fire and casualty insurance and, where circumstances warrant, flood insurance.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">&#160;</div></div>
<div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; WIDTH: 100%">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">9</font></div>
<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
<hr style="COLOR: gainsboro" align="left" noshade size="2" width="100%"></div></div>
<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right">&#160;</div></div></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Land Loans.</font>&#160;&#160;In 2005, we began to originate land loans based on our increased construction loan activity.&#160;&#160;At September 30, 2009, $45.0
million, or 10.4% of our total loans receivable consisted of land loans.&#160;&#160;Our land loans are made generally in conjunction with anticipated construction loan financing.&#160;&#160;The highest combined exposure is $11.6 million.&#160;&#160;In most cases the value of the land represents the borrower&#8217;s up-front equity in our construction loans.&#160;&#160;When the land value exceeds the borrower&#8217;s equity requirement, which is usually 25% of total project costs, including land, we will consider
originating this type of land loan.&#160;&#160;The majority of our land loans are referred by mortgage brokers who make the initial contact with the potential borrower and forward to us additional loan information that we review to determine whether the applicant satisfies our underwriting criteria.&#160;&#160;If the loan information meets our criteria, we issue a letter of intent listing the terms and conditions of any potential loan.&#160;&#160;If the potential borrower agrees to these terms and conditions,
we will continue our standard underwriting practice.&#160;&#160;We currently offer primarily adjustable rate residential land loans.&#160;&#160;At September 30, 2009, our largest land loan balance was $7.9 million, and the average land loan balance was $1.6 million.&#160;&#160;Land loans are generally repaid at the end of a two-year period.&#160;&#160;These loans generally have interest rates that adjust daily in conjunction with the prime rate and generally will not have an interest rate that adjusts below the
initial interest rate.&#160;&#160;Land loans will generally be made in amounts of up to 75% of the appraised value. <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Bank agreed with the OTS that, other than contractual commitments entered into prior to December 3, 2009, the Bank will not originate any land loans without prior OTS approval.</font></font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Land loans generally involve a greater degree of credit risk than one- to four-family residential mortgage loans.&#160;&#160;The risk of loss on a land loan depends upon the accuracy of the initial estimate of the value of the property as well as being able to complete development on a timely basis.&#160;&#160;For all loans, we utilize
outside independent appraisers approved by our board of directors.&#160;&#160;All borrowers are required to obtain title insurance.&#160;&#160;We also require fire and casualty insurance and, where circumstances warrant, flood insurance.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Other Loans</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">.&#160;&#160;</font>We offer loans that are either
unsecured or secured by property other than real estate.&#160;&#160;These loans include loans secured by deposits and personal loans.&#160;&#160;At September 30, 2009, these other loans totaled $684,000 or 0.2% of the loans receivable portfolio.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Loan Approval Procedures and Authorit</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">y</font>.&#160;&#160;The
loan approval process is intended to assess the borrower&#8217;s ability to repay the loan, the viability of the loan, and the adequacy of the value of the property that will secure the loan.&#160;&#160;To assess the borrower&#8217;s ability to repay, we review each borrower&#8217;s employment and credit history and information on the historical and projected income and expenses of mortgagors.&#160;&#160;All one- to four-family mortgage loans up to $850,000 must be approved by two members of the Management Loan
Committee, which is comprised of senior corporate officers, including the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer.&#160;&#160;All other mortgage loans up to $850,000 must be approved by two of the following officers:&#160;&#160;the President, the Chief Lending Officer, the Senior Vice President and the Manager of Residential Lending.&#160;&#160;All loans in excess of $850,000 must be approved by the Directors&#8217; Loan Committee.&#160;&#160;In addition, the board of directors ratifies all loans
approved by management including those approved by the Management Loan Committee.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Non-Performing Loans and Potential Problem Assets</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">After a one- to four-family residential loan becomes 15 days late, we deliver a computer-generated late charge notice to the borrower.&#160;&#160;Approximately one week later, we deliver a reminder notice.&#160;&#160;When a loan becomes 30 days delinquent, the loan servicing department manager determines whether to send an acceleration
letter to the borrower and attempts to make personal contact.&#160;&#160;After 60 days, we will generally refer the matter to legal counsel who is authorized to commence foreclosure proceedings.&#160;&#160;Management is authorized to begin foreclosure proceedings on any loan after 60 days, after determining that it is prudent to do so and the proper acceleration letter has been sent.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">After a multi-family, commercial real estate or construction loan becomes 10 days delinquent, we deliver a computer-generated late charge notice to the borrower and attempt to make personal contact with the borrower.&#160;&#160;If there is no successful resolution of the delinquency at that time, we may accelerate the payment terms of
the loan and issue a letter notifying the borrower of this acceleration.&#160;&#160;After such a loan is 15 days delinquent, we may refer the matter to legal counsel who is authorized to commence foreclosure proceedings.&#160;&#160;Management is authorized to begin foreclosure proceedings on any loan after determining that it is prudent to do so.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Mortgage loans are reviewed on a regular basis by management&#8217;s Asset Classification Committee and are placed on non-accrual status when they become 90 days or more delinquent and collection is doubtful or when, regardless of how many days delinquent the loan is, other factors indicate that the collection of these amounts is doubtful.&#160;&#160;When
loans are placed on non-accrual status, unpaid accrued interest is reversed, and further income is recognized only to the extent received.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">&#160;</div></div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">10</font></div>
<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
<hr style="COLOR: gainsboro" align="left" noshade size="2" width="100%"></div></div>
<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right">&#160;</div></div></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Non-Performing Loans.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font>Non-performing loans are
either in non-accrual status and/or past contractual maturity date.&#160;&#160;At September 30, 2009, $22.1 million of our loans net of specific allowances, or 5.13% of our total loans, were non-accrual and/or past maturity and therefore non-performing.&#160;&#160;These loans consist of multi-family, commercial real estate, construction and land loans.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Non-Performing Assets.&#160;&#160;</font>The table below sets forth the amounts and categories of our non-performing assets, net of specific allowances at the dates
indicated.&#160;&#160;We may from time to time agree to modify the contractual terms of a borrower&#8217;s loan.&#160;&#160;In cases where these modifications represent a concession (for which a portion of interest or principal has been forgiven and loans modified at interest rates materially less than current market rates) to a borrower experiencing financial difficulty, the modification is considered a troubled debt restructuring.&#160;&#160; At September 30, 2009, loans modified in a troubled debt restructuring
totaled $0.4 million.&#160;&#160;These loans were performing loans at the time their terms were modified and are performing in accordance with their new terms.&#160;&#160;Therefore, they are not included in the table below.&#160;&#160;For the periods presented from September 2005 through 2008, we had no troubled debt restructurings.&#160;&#160;The recent sharp deterioration in the real estate market has resulted in a deterioration of the Bank&#8217;s loans receivable portfolio, which in turn has caused increases
in non-performing loans.&#160;&#160;At September 30, 2009, nine loans totaling $22.1 million were in non-performing status versus two loans totaling $2.0 million in non-performing status at September 30, 2008.</font></font></div>

<td valign="bottom" width="6%" style="BORDER-BOTTOM: #000000 4px double; TEXT-ALIGN: right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">2</font></td>
<td nowrap valign="bottom" width="1%" style="PADDING-BOTTOM: 4px; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160;</font></td>

<td valign="bottom" width="1%" style="BORDER-BOTTOM: #000000 4px double; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">$</font></td>
<td valign="bottom" width="6%" style="BORDER-BOTTOM: #000000 4px double; TEXT-ALIGN: right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">652</font></td>
<td nowrap valign="bottom" width="1%" style="PADDING-BOTTOM: 4px; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160;</font></td></tr></table></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">For the fiscal year ended September 30, 2009, there was $0.7 million in interest income that would have been recorded had our non-accruing loans been current in accordance with their original terms.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Classified Assets.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font>Office of Thrift Supervision
regulations and our Asset Classification Policy provide that loans and other assets should be classified as &#8220;substandard,&#8221; &#8220;doubtful&#8221; or &#8220;loss&#8221; assets where a significant question as to collectability arises.&#160;&#160;An asset is considered &#8220;substandard&#8221; if it is inadequately protected by the current net worth and paying capacity of the obligor or of the collateral pledged, if any. &#8220;Substandard&#8221; assets include those characterized by the &#8220;distinct
possibility&#8221; that the institution will sustain &#8220;some loss&#8221; if the deficiencies are not corrected.&#160;&#160;Assets classified as &#8220;doubtful&#8221; have all of the weaknesses inherent in those classified &#8220;substandard,&#8221; with the added characteristic that the weaknesses present make &#8220;collection or liquidation in full,&#8221; on the basis of currently existing facts, conditions, and values, &#8220;highly questionable and improbable.&#8221; Assets classified as &#8220;loss&#8221;
are those considered &#8220;uncollectible&#8221; and of such little value that they should be entirely charged-off.&#160;&#160;We classify an asset as &#8220;special mention&#8221; if the asset has a potential weakness that warrants management&#8217;s close attention.&#160;&#160;While &#8220;special mention&#8221; assets have not deteriorated to the point of being classified as &#8220;substandard,&#8221; management has concluded that if the potential weakness in the asset is not addressed, the value of the asset
may deteriorate, thereby adversely affecting the repayment of the asset.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"></font><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">An institution is required to establish general allowances for loan losses in an amount deemed prudent by management for loans classified as &#8220;special mention.&#8221;&#160;&#160;General
allowances represent loss allowances which have been established to recognize the inherent losses associated with lending activities, but which, unlike specific allowances, have not been allocated to particular problem assets.&#160;&#160;When an institution classifies assets as &#8220;substandard or doubtful&#8221;, it is required either to establish a specific allowance for losses equal to the amount its internal analysis determines the potential loss to be on the asset or to charge off the amount.&#160;&#160;When
an institution classifies problem assets as &#8220;loss,&#8221; it is required either to establish a specific allowance for losses equal to 100% of the amount of the asset so classified or deemed uncollectable to charge off the amount.&#160;&#160;An institution&#8217;s determination as to the classification of its assets and the amount of its valuation allowances is subject to review by the Office of Thrift Supervision which can order the establishment of additional general or specific loss allowances.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right">&#160;</div></div></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"></font><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On the basis of management&#8217;s review of assets, at September 30, 2009, we classified $56.4 million of our assets as special mention or potential problem loans compared to $5.4 million
at September 30, 2008.&#160;&#160;This increase was due to the recent sharp deterioration in the real estate market that resulted in a deterioration of the Bank&#8217;s loans receivable portfolio.&#160;&#160;In addition, at September 30, 2009 we classified $54.4&#160;million as substandard compared to $6.8 million at September 30, 2008.&#160;&#160;We have provided $5.1 million in specific allowances for $23.0 million of the loans classified as substandard, which were comprised of five commercial real estate loans
(consisting of three relationships), one multi-family loan and one land loan.&#160;&#160;We classified as doubtful one unsecured consumer loan for $16,000 and provided $16,000 in specific allowance.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The first commercial real estate relationship consists of two loans having an aggregate outstanding balance of $9.8 million which are secured by fee and leasehold mortgage on two adjoining properties. These loans are currently in default and the Company is recording a $2.3 million specific allowance for potential foreclosure costs.&#160;&#160;The
loans are cross-collateralized and have a current appraised value of $8.8 million. The second relationship also consists of two loans with an aggregate balance of $5.3 million that are secured by an industrial warehouse. These loans are currently in default and the Company is recording a $0.8 million specific allowance based upon the properties&#8217; current appraised value of $5.6 million and potential foreclosure costs.&#160;&#160;The third relationship is a $0.3 million loan for which the Company is recording
a $30,000 specific allowance for potential foreclosure costs.&#160;&#160;The property was appraised at approximately $4.0 million in 2004 and the Company is awaiting receipt of a new appraisal. The multi-family loan is a $1.9 million loan secured by vacant corner residential property in Manhattan for which the Company is recording a $1.0 million specific allowance based on the property&#8217;s current appraised value and anticipated foreclosure costs.&#160;&#160;The Company is also recording a $1.0 million specific
allowance on a $5.7 million land loan which was prompted by a decrease in the current appraised value of the property.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The loan portfolio is reviewed on a regular basis by management&#8217;s Asset Classification Committee to determine whether any loans require classification in accordance with applicable regulations.&#160;&#160;Not all classified assets constitute non-performing assets.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Allowance for Loan Losses</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"></font><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our allowance for loan losses is intended to be maintained at a level necessary to absorb loan losses that are both probable and reasonably estimable.&#160;&#160;Management, in determining
the allowance for loan losses, considers the losses inherent in its loan portfolio and changes in the nature and volume of loan activities, along with the general economic and real estate market conditions.&#160;&#160;We utilize a two-tier approach: (1) identification of impaired loans and establishment of specific loss allowances on impaired loans, if any; and (2) establishment of general valuation allowances on the remainder of our loan portfolio.&#160;&#160;We maintain a loan review system, which provides
for a periodic review of our loan portfolio and the identification of potential impaired loans.&#160;&#160;This system takes into consideration, among other things, delinquency status, size of loans, type and market value of collateral and financial condition of the borrowers.&#160;&#160;Specific loan loss allowances are established for identified losses based on a review of this information.&#160;&#160;A loan evaluated for impairment is considered to be impaired when, based on current information and events,
it is probable that we will be unable to collect all amounts due according to the contractual terms of the loan agreement.&#160;&#160;We do not aggregate these loans for evaluation purposes.&#160;&#160;Loan impairment is measured based on the present value of expected future cash flows discounted at the loan&#8217;s effective interest rate or, as a practical expedient, at the loan&#8217;s observable market price or the fair value of the collateral if the loan is collateral dependent.&#160;&#160;General loan loss
allowances are based upon a combination of factors including, but not limited to, actual loan loss experience, composition of the loan portfolio, current economic conditions and management&#8217;s judgment.&#160;&#160;The allowance is increased through provisions charged against current earnings and recoveries of previously charged-off loans.&#160;&#160;Loans that are determined to be uncollectible are charged against the allowance.&#160;&#160;While management uses available information to recognize probable
and reasonably estimable loan losses, future loss provisions may be necessary based on changing economic conditions, particularly in the real estate sector.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">13</font></div>
<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
<hr style="COLOR: gainsboro" align="left" noshade size="2" width="100%"></div></div>
<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right">&#160;</div></div></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">A federally chartered savings association&#8217;s determinations as to the classification of its assets, charge-offs and the amount of its valuation allowances are subject to review by the Office of Thrift Supervision.&#160;&#160;The Office of Thrift Supervision, in conjunction with the other federal banking
agencies, provides guidance for financial institutions on both the responsibilities of management for the assessment and establishment of adequate valuation allowances and guidance for banking agency examiners to use in determining the adequacy of valuation allowances.&#160;&#160;All institutions are required to have effective systems and controls to identify, monitor and address asset quality problems, analyze all significant factors that affect the collectability of the portfolio in a reasonable manner and
establish acceptable allowance evaluation processes that meet the objectives of the federal regulatory agencies.&#160;&#160;There can be no assurance that the Office of Thrift Supervision, as a result of reviewing our loan portfolio and/or allowance, will not request that we alter our allowance for loan losses or require additional charge-offs, thereby affecting our financial condition and earnings.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Allowance for loan losses increased by $8.5 million, to $10.7 million for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2009 from $2.2 million for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2008.&#160;&#160;The increase is primarily the result of a $5.1 million increase in the specific allowances for impaired loans and a $3.4 million increase in general
allowances for increases in its loan receivable portfolio, loans classified as special mention and the general decline in economic conditions in our lending footprint.&#160;&#160;Over the last four years, there were no charge-offs or recoveries.</font>
<br><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The loan loss provision also increased $8.1 million to $8.5 million for fiscal year 2009 compared to $0.4 million for fiscal year 2008.&#160;&#160;The increase is primarily the result of a $5.1 million increase in the specific allowances on five commercial real estate loans (consisting of three relationships), one multi-family loan and
one land loan, as described in the prior section titled &#8220;Business-Classified Assets.&#8221; The remaining $3.0 million increase in loan loss provision was attributable to a) the transfer of $200.5 million from its held-for-sale loan portfolio to its loan receivable portfolio during the current fiscal year, b) the increase in potential problem loans, and c) the general decline in economic conditions on the balance of the loan receivable portfolio.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The transfer of the held-for-sale portfolio was due to the increased tightening in the credit markets, which has hampered the Company&#8217;s ability to sell these loans.&#160;&#160;Management decided to transfer these loans to its loans receivable portfolio and in accordance with its allowance for loan and lease losses policy established
a general provision.&#160;&#160;Loans held-for-sale are carried at the lower of cost or market and therefore do not require a general allowance for loan losses.&#160;&#160;The Company also increased its general provision due to an increase of $51.0 million in potential problem loans.&#160;&#160;Potential problem loans are loans that may or may not be delinquent.&#160;&#160;These are loans that the Company has identified as showing characteristics of potential inability on the part of the borrower to make payments
in accordance with the terms of the loan agreement.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"></font><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We have charged-off one consumer loan with a balance of $1,000 since fiscal year 2005.&#160;&#160;We have not charged-off a real estate mortgage loan since 2001, due in part, to what
has been, until recently, a stable local economy, prudent underwriting of loans and continuous monitoring of the loan portfolio to attempt to identify and address non-performing loans and potential problem assets at an early date.<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font>The amount of foreclosures we incurred in the last five years was not material to our consolidated financial statements taken as a whole and the Bank suffered no losses on foreclosed
assets during that period.&#160;&#160;The recent sharp deterioration in the real estate market, however, has resulted in a deterioration of the Bank&#8217;s loan portfolio, including increases in non-performing loans and problem assets, and will lead to charge-offs.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Allocation of Allowance for Loan Losses.&#160;&#160;</font>The following table sets forth the allowance for loan losses allocated by loan category, the percentage
of the allowance for loan losses in each category to the total allowance for loan losses, and the percent of loans in each category to total loans at the dates indicated.&#160;&#160;The allowance for loan losses allocated to each category is not necessarily indicative of future losses in any particular category and does not restrict the use of the allowance to absorb losses in other categories.</font></font></div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right">&#160;</div></div></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Each quarter, management evaluates the total balance of the allowance for loan losses based on several factors that are reflective of the inherent losses in the loan portfolio.&#160;&#160;This process includes, but is not limited to, a periodic review of loan collectability in light of historical experience, the nature and volume of loan
activity, conditions that may affect the ability of the borrower to repay, the underlying value of collateral, if applicable, and economic conditions in our immediate market area.&#160;&#160;First, we group loans by delinquency status.&#160;&#160;All loans deemed impaired are evaluated individually, based primarily on the value of the collateral securing the loan.&#160;&#160;Specific loss allowances are established as required by this analysis.&#160;&#160;All loans for which a specific loss allowance has not
been assigned are segregated by type and delinquency status and a loss allowance is established by using loss experience data and management&#8217;s judgment concerning other matters it considers significant.&#160;&#160;The allowance is allocated to each category of loans based on the results of the above analysis.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">This analysis process is inherently subjective, as it requires us to make estimates that are susceptible to revisions as more information becomes available.&#160;&#160;Although we believe that we have established the allowance at levels to absorb probable and estimable losses, future additions may be necessary if economic or other conditions
continue to deteriorate in the future from the current environment.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Investments</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Investments and Mortgage-Backed Securities</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">.&#160;&#160;</font>Our
investment portfolio at September 30, 2009 included $66.2 million of mortgage-backed securities, all of which are classified as held to maturity, and $2.4 million of Federal Home Loan Bank of New York stock.&#160;&#160;In addition, our investment portfolio at September 30, 2009 included $3.3 million of mutual fund shares, comprised primarily of a $2.8 million ultra-short term mutual fund classified as available-for-sale.&#160;&#160;Our investment policy objectives are to maintain liquidity within the guidelines
established by the board of directors.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"></font><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At September 30, 2009, we held $20.5 million of mortgage-backed securities issued by Freddie Mac and Fannie Mae, which are United States government-sponsored enterprises.&#160;&#160;The
remaining $45.7&#160;million of our mortgage-backed securities represents securities of private issuers and United States government agencies.&#160;&#160;Private issuer securities typically offer rates above those paid on securities of government-sponsored enterprises, but lack the guaranty of those enterprises and are often less liquid.&#160;&#160;The government-sponsored enterprises&#8217; portion of the mortgage-backed securities portfolio consisted of $16.8 million in fixed-rate mortgage-backed securities
and $3.7 million in adjustable rate mortgage-backed securities.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">For further discussion of our securities portfolio, please see Note 3 of Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements in Item 8, &#8220;Financial Statements and Supplementary Data.&#8221;</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Sources of Funds</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"></font><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">General.&#160;&#160;</font>Deposits have traditionally been our primary
source of funds for our lending and investment activities.&#160;&#160;In addition to deposits, funds are derived from scheduled loan payments, investment maturities, loan prepayments and income on earning assets.&#160;&#160;While scheduled loan payments and income on earning assets have been relatively stable sources of funds, deposit inflows and outflows can vary widely and are influenced by prevailing interest rates, market conditions and levels of competition. Borrowings from the Federal Home Loan Bank of
New York may be used to compensate for reductions in deposits and to fund loan and securities growth.&#160;&#160;As of September 30, 2009, we had $27.3 million of borrowings outstanding from the Federal Home Loan Bank of New York.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"></font><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Deposits.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font>Substantially
all of our depositors are persons who work or reside in Kings, Nassau or Suffolk Counties, New York.&#160;&#160;We offer a variety of deposit instruments.&#160;&#160;These include demand deposits consisting of non-interest bearing checking accounts, NOW accounts, money market accounts, passbook savings and club accounts, and fixed-term certificates of deposit.&#160;&#160;Deposit account terms vary, with the principal differences being the minimum balance required, the amount of time the funds must remain on deposit
and the interest rate.&#160;&#160;We do not have any brokered deposits at this time.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"></font><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We establish and adjust periodically the interest rates paid, maturity terms, service fees and withdrawal penalties on our deposits.&#160;&#160;Deposit rates and terms are based primarily
on current operating strategies and market rates, liquidity requirements, rates paid by competitors and growth goals. We rely on personalized customer service and long-standing relationships with customers to attract and retain deposits.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"></font><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The flow of deposits is influenced significantly by general economic conditions, changes in money market and other prevailing interest rates and competition.&#160;&#160;The variety of
deposit accounts offered allows us to be competitive in obtaining funds and responding to changes in consumer demand.&#160;&#160;Based on experience, management believes that our deposits are relatively stable.&#160;&#160;However, our ability to attract and maintain certificates of deposit, and the rates paid on these deposits, have been and will continue to be significantly affected by market conditions.&#160;&#160;At September 30, 2009, $250.8 million, or 62.38%, of our deposit accounts were certificates of
deposit, of which $190.8 million had maturities of one year or less.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Deposit Accounts</font>.&#160;&#160;The following table sets forth the distribution of total deposit accounts, by account type, at the dates indicated.</font></font></div>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
