<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Subsidiary Activities</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"></font><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Office of Thrift Supervision regulations permit federal savings associations to invest in the capital stock, obligations or other specified types of securities of subsidiaries (referred
to as &#8220;service corporations&#8221;) and to make loans to service corporations and joint ventures in which service corporations&#160;&#160;are participants in an aggregate amount not exceeding 2% of the association&#8217;s assets, plus an additional 1% of assets if the amount over 2% is used for specified community or inner-city development purposes.&#160;&#160;Service corporations may engage in certain activities not otherwise permissible for the Company but may not take deposits.&#160;&#160;In addition,
Federal regulations permit associations to make specified types of loans to service corporations&#160;&#160;(other than special-purpose finance subsidiaries) in which the association owns more than 10% of the stock, in an aggregate amount not exceeding 50% of the association&#8217;s regulatory capital if the association&#8217;s regulatory capital is in compliance with applicable regulations.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"></font><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">3D Holding Company was incorporated in New York in 1993, for the purpose of acquiring, managing, and disposing of real estate held by the Bank.&#160;&#160;As of September 30, 2009, the
subsidiary did not hold any real estate owned.&#160;&#160;As of September 30, 2009, total assets of 3D Holding Company were $158,000, and consisted solely of cash at that date.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"></font><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">BFS REIT, Inc. was incorporated in New York in 1999.&#160;&#160;The corporation is a wholly-owned subsidiary created for the purpose of acquiring, holding, and investing in certain real
estate-related loans and other assets that constitute permissible investments by the Bank.&#160;&#160;As of September 30, 2009, BFS REIT, Inc.&#8217;s total aggregate assets were $91.1 million.</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Personnel</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As of September 30, 2009, we had 74 full-time employees and 30 part-time employees.&#160;&#160;Our employees are not represented by any collective bargaining group.&#160;&#160;Management believes that we have good relations with our employees.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">FEDERAL, STATE AND LOCAL TAXATION</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">General.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font>The Bank&#8217;s Federal and state tax returns
have not been audited during the past five years.&#160;&#160;At this time the Company&#8217;s New York City tax returns are being audited for the 2005, 2006 and 2007 tax years.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Federal Taxation</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">General.&#160;&#160;</font>The Company and the Bank are subject to Federal income taxation in the same general manner as other corporations, with some exceptions
discussed below.&#160;&#160;The Company and the Bank file consolidated income tax returns.&#160;&#160;The following discussion of Federal taxation is intended only to summarize certain pertinent Federal income tax matters and is not a comprehensive description of the tax rules applicable to the Company or the Bank.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Method of Accounting</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">.&#160;&#160;</font>For Federal income
tax purposes, the Bank and Company report their income and expenses on the accrual method of accounting and use a tax year ending September 30 for filing Federal income tax returns.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Bad Debt Reserve and Recapture.&#160;&#160;</font>Prior to the Small Business Protection Act of 1996 (the &#8220;1996 Act&#8221;), the Bank was permitted to establish
a reserve for bad debts and to make annual additions to the reserve.&#160;&#160;These additions could, within specified formula limits, be deducted in arriving at our taxable income.&#160;&#160;The Bank was required to use the specific charge off method (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic">i.e.<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic">,</font></font> to claim a deduction equal to its actual loan loss experience) in computing its bad debt deduction beginning with its 1996 Federal tax return.&#160;&#160;The Bank was required
to recapture any excess reserves established after December 31, 1987.&#160;&#160;&#160;The Bank now maintains a frozen reserve equal to the balance of the bad debt reserves as of December 31, 1987 (the &#8220;base year reserve&#8221;).</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As more fully discussed below, the Bank files a New York State franchise tax return.&#160;&#160;New York State and New York City enacted legislation in 1996, which among other things, decoupled the Federal tax laws in connection with thrift bad debt deductions and continued to permit the use of the bad debt provisions that applied under
Federal law prior to the enactment of the 1996 Act.&#160;&#160;Provided the Bank continues to satisfy certain definitional tests and other conditions, for New York State and New York City income tax purposes, it is permitted to continue to use a reserve method for bad debt deductions.&#160;&#160;The deductible annual addition to such reserves may be computed using a specific formula based on an institution&#8217;s loss history (the &#8220;experience method&#8221;) or a statutory percentage equal to 32% of its
New York State and New York City taxable income (the &#8220;percentage method&#8221;) before bad debt deduction.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">

<hr style="COLOR: gainsboro" noshade size="1"></div></div>
<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right">&#160;</div></div></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Taxable Distributions and Recapture.&#160;&#160;</font>As described above, the 1996 Act modified the methods by which the Bank computes its bad debt deduction and
the Bank now maintains a frozen base year reserve. The base year reserve is subject to recapture if the Bank makes certain non-dividend distributions. In such cases, an amount based on the amounts distributed will be includable into the Bank&#8217;s taxable income.&#160;&#160;&#8220;Non-dividend distributions&#8221; include distributions in excess of the Bank&#8217;s current and accumulated earnings and profits, as calculated for federal income tax purposes; distributions in redemption of its stock; and distributions
in partial or complete liquidation.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At September 30, 2009, our total Federal pre-1988 base year tax bad debt reserve was approximately $1.6 million.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Alternative Minimum Tax</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">.&#160;&#160;</font>The Internal Revenue
Code of 1986, as amended (the &#8220;Code&#8221;) imposes an alternative minimum tax (&#8220;AMT&#8221;) at a rate of 20% on a base of regular taxable income plus certain tax preferences (&#8220;alternative minimum taxable income&#8221; or &#8220;AMTI&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The AMT is payable to the extent such AMTI is in excess of an exemption amount and the AMT exceeds the regular income tax.&#160;&#160;Net operating losses can offset no more than 90% of AMTI.&#160;&#160;Certain payments of AMT may be used as
credits against regular tax liabilities in future years.&#160;&#160;The Bank has not been subject to the AMT and has no such amounts available as credits for carryover.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Net Operating Loss Carryovers.&#160;&#160;</font>The Company may carry back net operating losses to the preceding two taxable years and forward to the succeeding
20 taxable years.&#160;&#160;The Worker, Homeownership, and Business Assistance Act of 2009 generally allows the Bank to elect a 3, 4, or 5-year carry-back period on net operating losses incurred in either 2008 or 2009. At September 30, 2009, the Company had no net operating loss carry-forwards for Federal income tax purposes.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Corporate Dividends-Received Deduction</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">.&#160;&#160;</font>The
Company may exclude from its income 100% of dividends received from the Bank as a member of the same affiliated group of corporations.&#160;&#160;The corporate dividends-received deduction is 80% in the case of dividends received from corporations with which a corporate recipient does not file a consolidated return, and corporations which own less than 20% of the stock of a corporation distributing a dividend may deduct only 70% of dividends received or accrued on their behalf.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">State and Local Taxation</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">New York State Taxation.&#160;&#160;</font>The Company and the Bank are subject to the New York State banking corporation tax.&#160;&#160;This tax is imposed in
an amount equal to the greater of (a) 7.1% of &#8220;entire net income&#8221; allocable to New York State, (b) 3% of &#8220;alternative entire net income&#8221; allocable to New York State, (c) 0.01% of the average value of assets allocable to New York State, or (d) a nominal minimum tax.&#160;&#160;Entire net income is based on Federal taxable income, subject to certain modifications.&#160;&#160;Alternative entire net income is equal to entire net income without certain modifications.&#160;&#160;The Company
and the Bank are also subject to the New York State tax surcharge equal to 17.0% of the New York State banking corporation tax allocable to business activities carried on in the Metropolitan Commuter Transportation District.&#160;&#160;There may be a reform of the New York State banking corporation tax that would change the way in which the Company and the Bank&#8217;s New York States taxes are computed.&#160;&#160;Please see &#8220;State and Local Taxation&#8212;Possible New York State Legislative Changes&#8221;
below for additional discussion.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Dividends received by the Bank from BFS REIT, Inc., a real estate investment trust, are subject to a 60% dividends-received deduction, which generally results in only 40% of BFS REIT, Inc.&#8217;s earnings being subject to New York State tax. The possible reform of the New York State banking corporation tax mentioned above could eliminate
the 60% dividends-received deduction in future years.&#160;&#160;Please see &#8220;State and Local Taxation&#8212;Possible New York State Legislative Changes&#8221; below.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">New York City Taxation.&#160;&#160;</font>The Bank is also subject to the New York City banking corporation tax, which is&#160;&#160;calculated, subject to a New
York City income and expense allocation, on a similar basis as the New York State banking corporation tax.&#160;&#160;The New York City tax on entire net income is imposed at a 9.0% tax rate.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Bad Debt Reserves.&#160;&#160;</font>New York State and New York City enacted legislation in 1996, which among other things, decoupled from the Federal tax laws
in connection with bad debt deductions for thrifts and continued to permit the use of the bad debt provisions that applied under Federal tax law prior to the enactment of the 1996 Act.&#160;&#160;Provided the Bank continues to satisfy certain definitional tests of a thrift and a specified qualifying-assets ratio for New York State and New York City income tax purposes, it is permitted to continue to take deductions from entire net income for additions to reserves for losses on bad debts.&#160;&#160;The deductible
annual addition to such reserves may be computed using a specific formula based on an institution&#8217;s loss history (the &#8220;experience method&#8221;) or a statutory percentage equal to 32% of its New York State and New York City taxable income (the &#8220;percentage method&#8221;) before bad debt deduction.&#160;&#160;There may be a reform of the New York State banking corporation tax that could eliminate the use of our current bad debt reserve method.&#160;&#160;Please see &#8220;State and Local Taxation&#8212;Possible
New York State Legislative Changes&#8221; below for additional discussion.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">23</font></div>
<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
<hr style="COLOR: gainsboro" noshade size="1"></div></div>
<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right">&#160;</div></div></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Recapture of Bad Debt Reserves.&#160;&#160;</font>Bad debt reserves consist of a defined &#8220;base-year&#8221; amount, plus additional amounts accumulated after
the base year.&#160;&#160;As of September 30, 2009, our New York State and New York City pre-1988 base-year reserve for the purposes of calculating any recapture of bad debt reserves was approximately $2.6 million.&#160;&#160;Under current New York State and New York City tax laws, bad debt reserves are subject to recapture if the Bank (i) makes certain &#8220;non-dividend distributions&#8221; or (ii) ceases to satisfy certain definitional tests of a thrift and fails to maintain a specified qualifying-assets
ratio.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Possible New York State Legislative Changes.&#160;&#160;</font>At the time of this filing, the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance is considering proposing
a legislative reform of the New York State corporate franchise and banking corporation tax rules.&#160;&#160;The proposed reform package that the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance has publicly released would substantially alter how the Company and the Bank are taxed in New York State and may materially increase their combined effective New York State tax rate.&#160;&#160;In particular, the current proposal by the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance would eliminate the 60% dividends-received
deduction for dividends the Bank receives from BFS REIT, Inc. as described above under &#8220;State and Local Taxation &#8211; New York State Taxation&#8221;, which would increase the portion of those dividends subject to New York State tax.&#160;&#160;Also, as described above under &#8220;State and Local Taxation &#8211; Bad Debt Reserves&#8221;, the current proposal may also require the Bank to utilize a different bad debt reserve method than the method it is currently using, which may result in an increase
in the Bank&#8217;s New York State taxes. More specifically, the proposal would re-couple New York State&#8217;s treatment of bad debt reserves and deductions with the Federal tax treatment after the 1996 Act so that the Bank would be entitled to claim a deduction equal only to its actual loan loss experience.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">It is not possible to predict whether the Department of Taxation and Finance&#8217;s proposal will be included in the New York State Governor&#8217;s Proposed Budget for 2010 (expected to be released in January 2010), whether any tax reform legislation will actually be proposed in the New York State legislature, whether any such legislation
would be enacted, how any enacted legislation would differ from the current law or the most current proposal released by the Department of Taxation and Finance, and how any such legislative changes would impact the Company and the Bank&#8217;s effective New York State tax rate.&#160;&#160;It is also uncertain at this time whether there would be any similar changes made to the New York City banking corporation tax.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">SUPERVISION AND REGULATION</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">General</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Bank is examined and supervised by the Office of Thrift Supervision.&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Bank also is regulated to a lesser extent by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, governing reserves to be maintained against deposits and other matters, and
the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation as the insurer of deposit accounts.&#160;&#160;</font>This regulation and supervision establishes a comprehensive framework of activities in which an institution may engage and is intended primarily for the protection of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation&#8217;s deposit insurance funds and depositors.&#160;&#160;Under this system of Federal regulation, financial institutions are periodically examined to ensure that they satisfy applicable standards with respect
to their capital adequacy, assets, management, earnings, liquidity and sensitivity to market interest rates.&#160;&#160;Following completion of its examination, the Federal agency critiques the institution&#8217;s operations and assigns its rating (known as an institution&#8217;s CAMELS rating).&#160;&#160;Under Federal law, an institution may not disclose its CAMELS rating to the public.&#160;&#160;The Bank also is a member of and owns stock in the Federal Home Loan Bank of New York, which is one of the 12 regional
banks in the Federal Home Loan Bank System.&#160;&#160;The Office of Thrift Supervision examines the Bank and prepares reports for the consideration of its board of directors on any operating deficiencies.&#160;&#160;The Bank&#8217;s relationship with its depositors and borrowers also is regulated to a great extent by both Federal and state laws, especially in matters concerning the ownership of deposit accounts and the form and content of the Bank&#8217;s mortgage documents.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right">&#160;</div></div></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Any change in these laws or regulations, whether by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, Office of Thrift Supervision<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System</font> or United States Congress, could have a material adverse impact on the Company
and the Bank and their operations.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Federal Banking Regulation</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Business Activities.&#160;&#160;</font>A federal savings association derives its lending and investment powers from the Home Owners&#8217; Loan Act, as amended,
and the regulations of the Office of Thrift Supervision.&#160;&#160;Under these laws and regulations, the Bank may originate mortgage loans secured by residential and commercial real estate, commercial business and consumer loans, and it may invest in certain types of debt securities and certain other assets.&#160;&#160;Certain types of lending, such as commercial and consumer loans, are subject to an aggregate limit calculated as a specified percentage of the Bank&#8217;s capital assets.&#160;&#160;The Bank
also may establish subsidiaries that may engage in activities not otherwise permissible for the Bank, including real estate investment and securities and insurance brokerage.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Capital Requirements.</font>&#160;&#160;Office of Thrift Supervision regulations require savings associations to meet three minimum capital standards:&#160;&#160;a
1.5% tangible capital ratio, a 4% leverage ratio (3% for associations receiving the highest CAMELS rating) and an 8% risk-based capital ratio.&#160;&#160;The prompt corrective action standards discussed below, in effect, establish a minimum 2% tangible capital standard.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The risk-based capital standard for savings associations requires the maintenance of Tier&#160;1 (core) and total capital (which is defined as core capital and supplementary capital) to risk-weighted assets of at least 4% and 8%, respectively.&#160;&#160;In determining the amount of risk-weighted assets, all assets, including certain off-balance
sheet assets, are multiplied by a risk-weight factor of 0% to 100% assigned by the Office of Thrift Supervision based on the risks believed inherent in the type of asset.&#160;&#160;Core capital is defined to include common stockholders&#8217; equity (including retained earnings), certain noncumulative perpetual preferred stock, certain accounts and deposits and related surplus and minority interests in equity accounts of consolidated subsidiaries, less <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">goodwill,
certain credit-enhancing credit only strips, certain deferred tax assets and</font> intangibles other than certain servicing assets and credit card relationships.&#160;&#160;The components of supplementary capital currently include cumulative preferred stock, long-term perpetual preferred stock, mandatory convertible securities, subordinated debt and intermediate preferred stock, the allowance for loan and lease losses limited to a maximum of 1.25% of risk-weighted assets and up to 45% of net unrealized gains
on available-for-sale equity securities with readily determinable fair market values.&#160;&#160;Overall, the amount of supplementary capital included as part of total capital cannot exceed 100% of core capital.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At September 30, 2009, the Bank&#8217;s capital exceeded all applicable requirements.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Loans to One Borrower.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font> A federal savings association
generally may not make a loan or extend credit to a single or related group of borrowers in excess of 15% of unimpaired capital and surplus.&#160;&#160;An additional amount may be loaned, equal to 10% of unimpaired capital and surplus, if the loan is secured by readily marketable collateral, which generally does not include real estate.&#160;&#160;As of September 30, 2009, the Bank was in compliance with the loans-to-one borrower limitations.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Qualified Thrift Lender Test.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font>As a federal savings
association, the Bank is subject to a qualified thrift lender, or &#8220;QTL,&#8221; test.&#160;&#160;Under the QTL test, the Bank must maintain at least 65% of its &#8220;portfolio assets&#8221; in &#8220;qualified thrift investments&#8221; in at least nine months of the most recent 12-month period.&#160;&#160;&#8220;Portfolio assets&#8221; generally means total assets of a savings institution, less the sum of specified liquid assets up to 20% of total assets, goodwill and other intangible assets, and the value
of property used in the conduct of the savings association&#8217;s business.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#8220;Qualified thrift investments&#8221; includes various types of loans made for residential and housing purposes, investments related to those purposes, including certain mortgage-backed and related securities, and loans for personal, family, household and certain other purposes up to a limit of 20% of portfolio assets.&#160;&#160;&#8220;Qualified
thrift investments&#8221; also include 100% of an institution&#8217;s credit card loans, education loans and small business loans.&#160;&#160;The Bank also may satisfy the QTL test by qualifying as a &#8220;domestic building and loan association&#8221; as defined in the Internal Revenue Code.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">A savings association that fails the qualified thrift lender test must either convert to a commercial bank charter or operate under specified restrictions.&#160;&#160;At September 30, 2009, the Bank maintained substantially all of its portfolio assets in qualified thrift investments.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Capital Distributions.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font>Office of Thrift Supervision
regulations govern capital distributions by a federal savings association, which include cash dividends, stock repurchases and other transactions charged to the capital account.&#160;&#160;A savings association must file an application for approval of a capital distribution if:</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">the distribution would violate any applicable statute, regulation, agreement or Office of Thrift Supervision-imposed condition; or</font></div></td></tr><tr>

<td align="left" valign="top" width="90%">
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">the association is not eligible for expedited treatment of its filings.</font></div></td></tr></table></div></div>
<div align="left">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Even if an application is not otherwise required, every savings association that is a subsidiary of a holding company must still file a notice with the Office of Thrift Supervision at least 30 days before the board of directors declares a dividend or approves a capital distribution.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Office of Thrift Supervision may disapprove a notice or application if:</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">
<div align="left">
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">

<td align="left" valign="top" width="5%">
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#9679;</font></div></td>
<td align="left" valign="top" width="90%">
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">the association would be undercapitalized following the distribution;</font></div></td></tr><tr>
<td valign="top" width="5%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160; </font></td>
<td valign="top" width="5%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160; </font></td>
<td valign="top" width="90%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160; </font></td></tr><tr>
<td valign="top" width="5%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160; </font></td>
<td align="left" valign="top" width="5%">
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#9679;</font></div></td>
<td align="left" valign="top" width="90%">
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">the proposed capital distribution raises safety and soundness concerns; or</font></div></td></tr><tr>
<td valign="top" width="5%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160; </font></td>
<td valign="top" width="5%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160; </font></td>
<td valign="top" width="90%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160; </font></td></tr><tr>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#9679;</font></div></td>
<td align="left" valign="top" width="90%">
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">the capital distribution would violate a prohibition contained in any statute, regulation or agreement.</font></div></td></tr></table></div></div>
<div>&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In addition, the Federal Deposit Insurance Act provides that an insured depository institution shall not make any capital distribution, if after making the distribution the institution would be undercapitalized.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Liquidity.</font>&#160;&#160;A federal savings association is required to maintain a sufficient amount of liquid assets to ensure its safe and sound operation.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Community Reinvestment Act and Fair Lending Laws.</font>&#160;&#160;All savings associations have a responsibility under the Community Reinvestment Act and related
regulations of the Office of Thrift Supervision to help meet the credit needs of their communities, including low- and moderate-income neighborhoods.&#160;&#160;In connection with its examination of a federal savings association, the Office of Thrift Supervision is required to assess the association&#8217;s record of compliance with the Community Reinvestment Act.&#160;&#160;In addition, the Equal Credit Opportunity Act and the Fair Housing Act prohibit lenders from discriminating in their lending practices on
the basis of characteristics specified in those statutes.&#160;&#160;An association&#8217;s failure to comply with the provisions of the Community Reinvestment Act could result in denial of certain corporate applications, such as branches or mergers, or restrictions on its activities.&#160;&#160;The failure to comply with the Equal Credit Opportunity Act and the Fair Housing Act could result in enforcement actions by the Office of Thrift Supervision, as well as other Federal regulatory agencies and the Department
of Justice.&#160;&#160;The Bank received a satisfactory Community Reinvestment Act rating in its most recent Federal examination.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Transactions with Related Parties.</font>&#160;&#160;A federal savings association&#8217;s authority to engage in transactions with its &#8220;affiliates&#8221;
is limited by Sections 23A and 23B of the Federal Reserve Act (the &#8220;FRA&#8221;) and its implementing regulations.&#160;&#160;The term &#8220;affiliates&#8221; for these purposes generally means any company that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with an institution.&#160;&#160;The Company is an affiliate of the Bank.&#160;&#160;In general, transactions with affiliates must be on terms that are as favorable to the association as comparable transactions with non-affiliates.&#160;&#160;In
addition, certain types of these transactions are restricted to an aggregate percentage of the association&#8217;s capital.&#160;&#160;Collateral in specified amounts must usually be provided by affiliates in order to receive loans from the association.&#160;&#160;In addition, Office of Thrift Supervision regulations prohibit a savings association from lending to any of its affiliates that are engaged in activities that are not permissible for bank holding companies and from purchasing the securities of any affiliate,
other than the shares of a subsidiary.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">&#160;</div></div>
<div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; WIDTH: 100%">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">26</font></div>
<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
<hr style="COLOR: gainsboro" noshade size="1"></div></div>
<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right">&#160;</div></div></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Bank&#8217;s authority to extend credit to its directors, executive officers and 10% shareholders (&#8220;Insiders&#8221;), as well as to entities controlled by insiders, is currently governed by the requirements of Sections&#160;22(g) and 22(h) of the FRA and Regulation O of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System.&#160;&#160;Among
other things, these provisions require that extensions of credit to Insiders (i) be made on terms that are substantially the same as, and follow credit underwriting procedures that are not less stringent than, those prevailing for comparable transactions with unaffiliated persons and that do not involve more than the normal risk of repayment or present other unfavorable features, and (ii) not exceed certain limitations on the amount of credit extended to Insiders, individually and in the aggregate, which limits
are based, in part, on the amount of the Bank&#8217;s capital.&#160;&#160;In addition, the Bank&#8217;s board of directors must approve extensions of credit in excess of certain limits.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Enforcement.</font>&#160;&#160;The Office of Thrift Supervision has primary enforcement responsibility over federal savings institutions and has the authority to
bring enforcement action against all &#8220;institution-affiliated parties,&#8221; including stockholders, attorneys, appraisers and accountants who knowingly or recklessly participate in wrongful action likely to have an adverse effect on an insured institution.&#160;&#160;Formal enforcement action may range from the issuance of a capital directive or cease and desist order to removal of officers and/or directors of the institution, receivership, conservatorship or the termination of deposit insurance.&#160;&#160;Civil
penalties cover a wide range of violations and actions, and range up to $25,000 per day, unless a finding of reckless disregard is made, in which case penalties may be as high as $1 million per day.&#160;&#160;The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation also has the authority to recommend to the Director of the Office of Thrift Supervision that enforcement action be taken with respect to a particular savings institution.&#160;&#160;If the Director does not take action, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation
has authority to take action under specified circumstances.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Standards for Safety and Soundness.</font>&#160;&#160;Federal law requires each federal banking agency to prescribe certain standards for all insured depository
institutions.&#160;&#160;These standards relate to, among other things, internal controls, information systems and audit systems, loan documentation, credit underwriting, interest rate risk exposure, asset growth, compensation, and other operational and managerial standards as the agency deems appropriate.&#160;&#160;The federal banking agencies adopted Interagency Guidelines Establishing Standards for Safety and Soundness to implement the safety and soundness standards required under Federal law.&#160;&#160;The
guidelines set forth the safety and soundness standards that the federal banking agencies use to identify and address problems at insured depository institutions before capital becomes impaired.&#160;&#160;The guidelines address internal controls and information systems, internal audit systems, credit underwriting, loan documentation, interest rate risk exposure, asset growth, compensation, fees and benefits.&#160;&#160;If the appropriate federal banking agency determines that an institution fails to meet any
standard prescribed by the guidelines, the agency may require the institution to submit to the agency an acceptable plan to achieve compliance with the standard.&#160;&#160;If an institution fails to meet these standards, the appropriate federal banking agency may require the institution to submit a compliance plan.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Prompt Corrective Action Regulations</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">.</font>&#160;&#160;Under
the prompt corrective action regulations, the Office of Thrift Supervision is required and authorized to take supervisory actions against undercapitalized savings associations.&#160;&#160;For this purpose, a savings association is placed in one of the following five categories based on the association&#8217;s capital:</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right">&#160;</div></div></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Generally, the banking regulator is required to appoint a receiver or conservator for an association that is &#8220;critically undercapitalized&#8221; within specific time frames.&#160;&#160;The regulations also provide that a capital restoration plan must be filed with the Office of Thrift Supervision within 45 days of the date an association
receives notice that it is &#8220;undercapitalized,&#8221; &#8220;significantly undercapitalized&#8221; or &#8220;critically undercapitalized,&#8221; the performance of which must be guaranteed by any company controlling the association up to specified limits.&#160;&#160;In addition, numerous mandatory supervisory actions become immediately applicable to the association, including, but not limited to, restrictions on growth, investment activities, capital distributions and affiliate transactions.&#160;&#160;The
Office of Thrift Supervision may also take any one of a number of discretionary supervisory actions against undercapitalized associations, including the issuance of a capital directive and the replacement of senior executive officers and directors.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At September 30, 2009, the Bank met the criteria for being considered &#8220;well-capitalized.&#8221;</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Insurance of Deposit Accounts.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font>Deposit accounts
in the Bank are insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, generally up to a maximum of $100,000 per separately insured depositor and up to a maximum of $250,000 for self-directed retirement accounts.&#160;&#160;However, pursuant to its statutory authority, the Board of Directors of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation increased the deposit insurance available on deposit accounts to $250,000 effective until December 31, 2013.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Bank&#8217;s deposits are subject to Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">(&#8220;FDIC&#8221;) </font>deposit insurance assessments. <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On March 4, 2009, the </font>FDIC revised its
risk-based system for determining deposit insurance assessments.&#160;&#160;This assessment is based on the risk category of the institution and <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">currently</font> ranges from <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">7 to 77.5</font> basis points of the institution&#8217;s deposits.&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">To determine the total base assessment
rate,</font> the FDIC first establishes an institution&#8217;s initial base assessment rate.&#160;&#160;This initial base assessment rate ranges, depending on the risk category of the institution, from 12 to 45 basis points.&#160;&#160;The FDIC then adjusts the initial base assessment (higher or lower) to obtain the total base assessment rate.&#160;&#160;The adjustments to the initial base assessment rate are based upon an institution&#8217;s levels of unsecured debt, secured liabilities, and brokered deposits.&#160;&#160;The
total base assessment rate would range from 7 to 77.5 basis points of the institution&#8217;s deposits.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On May 22, 2009, the FDIC adopted a final rule imposing a five basis point special assessment on each insured depository institution&#8217;s assets minus Tier 1 capital as of June 30, 2009. As a result, our expense for deposit insurance for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2009 includes approximately $0.2 million for this emergency
assessment which was levied as of June 30, 2009 and collected on September 30, 2009.&#160;&#160;The May 22nd final rule also permitted the FDIC to impose up to two additional special assessments of up to five basis points later in 2009 if necessary to maintain public confidence in federal deposit insurance.&#160;&#160;However, on September&#160;30, 2009, the FDIC filed a notice of proposed rulemaking, which was adopted as a final rule on November 12, 2009 and amended its assessment regulations to require insured
institutions to prepay, on December 30, 2009, their estimated quarterly risk-based assessments for the fourth quarter of calendar 2009 and for all of the calendar years 2010, 2011 and 2012.&#160;&#160;The amount of the prepayment generally will be determined based upon an institution&#8217;s assessment rate in effect on September 30, 2009 and will reflect a 5% annualized growth factor applied to the institution&#8217;s assessment base as well as an assessment rate increase of three cents per $100 of deposits
effective January 1, 2011.&#160;&#160;The Bank&#8217;s prepayment amount is $2.3 million.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In addition to the FDIC assessments, the Financing Corporation (&#8220;FICO&#8221;) is authorized to impose and collect, with the approval of the FDIC, assessments for anticipated payments, issuance costs and custodial fees on bonds issued by FICO in the 1980s to recapitalize
the former Federal Savings and Loan Insurance Corporation.&#160;&#160;The bonds issued by FICO are due to mature in 2017 through 2019.&#160;&#160;For the quarter ended September 30, 2009, the annualized FICO assessment was equal to 1.06 basis points for each $100 in domestic deposits maintained at an institution.&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Assessments related to the FICO bond obligations are not subject to the prepayment requirements.</font></font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Bank has opted in to the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation&#8217;s Transaction Guarantee Program and is</font> subject to a 0.10% surcharge applied to non-interest bearing transaction deposit
account balances in excess of $250,000, which surcharge <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">has been </font>added to the institution&#8217;s existing risk-based deposit insurance assessments.&#160;&#160;The Bank <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">has elected to continue </font>in the <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Transaction Guarantee</font> Program <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">through
June 30, 2010.</font></font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">28</font></div>
<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right">&#160;</div></div></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Prohibitions Against Tying Arrangements</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">.</font>&#160;&#160;Federal
savings associations are prohibited, subject to some exceptions, from extending credit to or offering any other service, or fixing or varying the consideration for an extension of credit or service, on the condition that the customer obtain some additional service from the institution or its affiliates or not obtain services of a competitor of the institution.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Federal Home Loan Bank System.</font>&#160;&#160;The Bank is a member of the Federal Home Loan Bank System, which consists of 12 regional Federal Home Loan Banks.&#160;&#160;The
Federal Home Loan Bank System provides a central credit facility primarily for member institutions.&#160;&#160;As a member of the Federal Home Loan Bank of New York, the Bank is required to acquire and hold shares of capital stock in the Federal Home Loan Bank in an amount <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">equal to the greater of </font>(i) $1,000 or (ii) 0.20% of the aggregate principal amount of its unpaid residential mortgage loans and similar obligations, also referred
to as Mortgage Related Assets (&#8220;MRA&#8221;), at the beginning of each year, plus 4.50% of the total dollar amount of its Advances (&#8220;borrowings&#8221;) and Mortgage Partnership Finance (&#8220;MPF&#8221;) transactions from the Federal Home Loan Bank, also referred to as the activity-based capital requirement, whichever is greater.&#160;&#160;During the year the activity-based capital requirement will increase or decrease depending on our activity with the Federal Home Loan Bank of New York.&#160;&#160;As
of September 30, 2009, the Bank was in compliance with this requirement.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Federal Reserve System</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Federal Reserve Board regulations require savings associations to maintain non-interest-earning reserves against their transaction accounts, such as negotiable orders of withdrawal (NOW) and regular checking accounts.&#160;&#160;At September 30, 2009, the Bank was in compliance with these reserve requirements.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The USA PATRIOT Act</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The USA PATRIOT Act of 2001 gave the federal government new powers to address terrorist threats through enhanced domestic security measures, expanded surveillance powers, increased information sharing and broadened anti-money laundering requirements.&#160;&#160;The USA PATRIOT Act also required the federal banking agencies to take into
consideration the effectiveness of controls designed to combat money laundering activities in determining whether to approve a merger or other acquisition application of a member institution.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, if we engage in a merger or other acquisition, our controls designed to combat money laundering would be considered as part of the application process.&#160;&#160;We have established policies, procedures and systems designed to comply with these regulations.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 was enacted in response to public concerns regarding corporate accountability in connection with certain accounting scandals.&#160;&#160;The stated goals of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act are to increase corporate responsibility, to provide for enhanced penalties for accounting and auditing improprieties at publicly
traded companies, and to protect investors by improving the accuracy and reliability of corporate disclosures pursuant to the securities laws. The Sarbanes-Oxley Act generally applies to all companies that file or are required to file periodic reports with the SEC, under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Sarbanes-Oxley Act includes specific additional disclosure requirements, requires the SEC and national securities exchanges to adopt extensive additional disclosure, corporate governance and other related rules, and mandates further studies of certain issues by the SEC.&#160;&#160;The Sarbanes-Oxley Act represents significant Federal
involvement in matters traditionally left to state regulatory systems, such as the regulation of the accounting profession, and to state corporate law, such as the relationship between a board of directors and management and between a board of directors and its committees.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">have incurred and </font>anticipate that we will <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">continue to</font> incur additional expense in complying with the provisions of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act and the regulations that have
been promulgated to implement the Sarbanes-Oxley Act, particularly those regulations relating to the establishment of internal controls over financial reporting.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Holding Company Regulation</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">General</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">.&#160;&#160;BFS </font>Bancorp<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">,
MHC and the Company are non-diversified savings and loan holding companies within the meaning of the Home Owners&#8217; Loan Act.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, BFS Bancorp, MHC and the Company are registered with the Office of Thrift Supervision and are subject to Office of Thrift Supervision regulations, examinations, supervision and reporting requirements.&#160;&#160;In addition, the Office of Thrift Supervision has enforcement authority over the Company and BFS Bancorp, MHC, and their subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;Among
other things, this authority permits the Office of Thrift Supervision to restrict or prohibit activities that are determined to be a serious risk to the subsidiary savings institution.&#160;&#160;As federal corporations, the Company and BFS Bancorp, MHC are generally not subject to state business organization laws.</font></font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Permitted Activities</font>.&#160;&#160;Pursuant to Section 10(o) of the Home Owners&#8217; Loan Act and Office of Thrift Supervision regulations and policy, a mutual
holding company and a federally chartered mid-tier holding company such as the Company may engage in the following activities: (i) investing in the stock of a savings association; (ii) acquiring a mutual association through the merger of the association into a savings association subsidiary of the holding company or an interim savings association subsidiary of the holding company; (iii) merging with or acquiring another holding company, one of whose subsidiaries is a savings association; (iv) investing in a corporation,
the capital stock of which is available for purchase by a savings association under Federal law or under the law of any state where the subsidiary savings association or associations share their home offices; (v) furnishing or performing management services for a savings association subsidiary of the company; (vi) holding, managing or liquidating assets owned or acquired from a savings subsidiary of the company; (vii) holding or managing properties used or occupied by a savings association subsidiary of the company;
(viii) acting as trustee under deeds of trust; (ix) any other activity (A) that the Federal Reserve Board, by regulation, has determined to be permissible for bank holding companies under Section 4(c) of the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, unless the Director, by regulation, prohibits or limits that activity for savings and loan holding companies; or (B) in which multiple savings and loan holding companies were authorized (by regulation) to directly engage on March 5, 1987; (x) any activity permissible for
financial holding companies under Section 4(k) of the Bank Holding Company Act, including securities and insurance underwriting; and (xi) purchasing, holding, or disposing of stock acquired in connection with a qualified stock issuance if the purchase of the stock by the savings and loan holding company is approved by the Director of the Office of Thrift Supervision.&#160;&#160;If a mutual holding company acquires or merges with another holding company, the holding company acquired or the holding company resulting
from the merger or acquisition may only invest in assets and engage in activities listed in (i) through (xi) above, and has a period of two years to cease any nonconforming activities and divest of any nonconforming investments.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Home Owners&#8217; Loan Act prohibits a savings and loan holding company, including the Company and BFS Bancorp, MHC, directly or indirectly, or through one or more subsidiaries, from acquiring more than 5% of another savings institution or holding company thereof, without prior written approval of the Office of Thrift Supervision.&#160;&#160;It
also prohibits the acquisition or retention of, with certain exceptions, more than 5% of a non-subsidiary company engaged in activities other than those permitted by the Home Owners&#8217; Loan Act; or acquiring or retaining control of an institution that is not federally insured.&#160;&#160;In evaluating applications by holding companies to acquire savings institutions, the Office of Thrift Supervision must consider the financial and managerial resources, future prospects of the company and institution involved,
the effect of the acquisition on the risk to the insurance fund, the convenience and needs of the community and competitive factors.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Office of Thrift Supervision is prohibited from approving any acquisition that would result in a multiple savings and loan holding company controlling savings institutions in more than one state, subject to two exceptions:&#160;&#160;(i) the approval of interstate supervisory acquisitions by savings and loan holding companies, and
(ii) the acquisition of a savings institution in another state if the laws of the state of the target savings institution specifically permit those acquisitions.&#160;&#160;The states vary in the extent to which they permit interstate savings and loan holding company acquisitions.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
