<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Certificates of Deposit.&#160;&#160;</font>Investments in certificates of deposit decreased by $1.4 million, or 100%, to zero at September 30, 2009 from $1.4 million
at September 30, 2008.&#160;&#160;This decrease was due to maturities of the certificates.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Securities.&#160;&#160;</font>Investment securities, which represent the available-for-sale and held-to-maturity portfolios, decreased $12.2 million, or 15.0%, to
$69.5 million at September 30, 2009, from $81.7 million at September 30, 2008.&#160;&#160;This decrease was primarily due to the repayments of mortgage-backed related securities, recording of an other-than-temporary impairment and repayments of other securities, offset by purchases of mortgage-backed related securities.&#160;&#160;Our holdings of mortgage-backed securities held-to-maturity and securities available-for-sale totaled $66.2&#160;million and $3.3 million, respectively, at September 30, 2009.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Loans receivable.&#160;&#160;</font>Loans
receivable before allowance for loan losses, which include deferred fees and loans held-for-sale increased $54.9 million, or 14.6%, to $430.4&#160;million at September 30, 2009 from $375.5 million at September 30, 2008.&#160;&#160;Loans held-for-sale decreased by $134.2 million, or 100%, to zero at September 30, 2009 from $134.2 million at September 30, 2008 and our loans receivable portfolio increased by $189.1 million, or 78.4%, to $430.4 million at September 30, 2009 from $241.3 million at September 30, 2008.&#160;&#160;Due
to the impact of the recent economic downturn and increased tightening in the credit markets affecting the Company&#8217;s ability to sell the loans in the held-for-sale portfolio during fiscal year 2009, the Company transferred $200.5 million in loans held-for-sale&#160;&#160;to the loans receivable portfolio.&#160;&#160;These loan transfers occurred throughout the fiscal year ended September 30, 2009 and are reflected in the loans receivable portfolio balances as of September 30, 2009.&#160;&#160;As of September
30, 2009, the Company held no loans in the loans held-for-sale portfolio.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Federal Home Loan Bank of New York Stock.&#160;&#160;</font>Federal Home Loan Bank<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font>of
New York stock decreased by $0.4 million, or 15.0%, to $2.4 million at September 30, 2009, from $2.8 million at September 30, 2008.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Bank-Owned Life Insurance.&#160;&#160;</font>Bank-owned life insurance increased $0.4 million, or 4.2%, to $9.5 million at September 30, 2009, from $9.1 million
at September 30, 2008.&#160;&#160;This increase was primarily due to the increase in the cash surrender value of the policies.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Accrued interest receivable.</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Accrued interest receivable increased $0.3 million, or 13.0%, to $2.8 million at September 30, 2009, from
$2.5 million at September 30, 2008.&#160;&#160;This increase was primarily due to the increase in the loans receivable portfolio.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Premises and equipment, net.</font>&#160;&#160;Premises and equipment decreased $0.3 million, or 11.2%, to $2.0 million at September 30, 2009, from $2.3 million
at September 30, 2008.&#160;&#160;The decrease was primarily due to the accumulated depreciation of $0.5 million offset by equipment purchases of $0.2 million.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Prepaid Expenses and Other Assets.&#160;&#160;</font>Prepaid expenses and other assets increased $6.5 million, or 114.3%, to $12.1 million at September 30, 2009,
from $5.6 million at September 30, 2008.&#160;&#160;The increase was primarily due to $7.3 million in the net deferred tax assets caused by the increase in temporary charges for other-than-temporary impairment on investment securities and the increase in provision for loan losses.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Deposits</font>.&#160;&#160;Deposits increased by $59.6 million, or 17.4%, to $402.1 million at September 30, 2009, from $342.5 million at September 30, 2008. The
increase was attributable to a $40.4&#160;million increase in certificates of deposit, an increase in other interest bearing deposits of $21.4 million, offset by a decrease in non-interest bearing deposits of $2.2 million.&#160;&#160;The net deposit inflow was primarily used to fund our mortgage loan portfolio.&#160;&#160;The Bank maintains marketing and promotional efforts in its market area, including efforts to remain competitive in all of its deposit offerings.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Borrowed Funds</font>.&#160;&#160;Borrowed funds from the Federal Home Loan Bank of New York decreased by $16.9 million, or 38.3%, to $27.3 million at September

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Non-interest Income</font>.&#160;&#160;Non-interest income decreased by $0.4 million, or 13.8% to $2.7&#160;million for fiscal year 2008, from $3.1 million for fiscal
year 2007.&#160;&#160;The decrease was primarily the result of an other-than-temporary charge of $1.3 million, offset by increases of $0.5 million in banking fees and service charges, $0.1 million in net gain on sale of loans held-for-sale and $0.3 million in other income.&#160;&#160;The increase in banking fees and service charges was primarily the result of increased loan syndication and other related loan fees earned of approximately $0.5 million, partially offset by a reduction in deposit related fees of
approximately $16,000.&#160;&#160;The increase in the net gain on sale of loans reflects the increased profits of loans sold including net gains for servicing rights.&#160;&#160;The increase in other income was primarily due to the proceeds received on the Bank Owned Life Insurance policies of approximately $0.2 million, Bank Owned Life Insurance income of $16,000, miscellaneous income of approximately $10,000 and depositor related fees of approximately $1,000, which include ATM fees, debit card fees and safe
deposit rental income.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: left">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: left">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Non-interest Expense</font>.&#160;&#160;Non-interest expense decreased by $2.6 million, or 18.7%, to $11.5&#160;million in fiscal year 2008 compared to $14.1 million
in fiscal year 2007.&#160;&#160;The largest component of the decrease was in compensation and fringe benefits.&#160;&#160;Compensation and fringe benefits decreased $2.9 million, or 27.7%, to $7.6 million for fiscal year 2008 from $10.5 million in fiscal year 2007.&#160;&#160;This decrease was primarily due to the stock-based incentive plan reduced expenses of $3.8 million, offset in part by increases in compensation of $0.8 million, which included general salary increases for officers and employees and hiring
of staff, health care expenses of $0.1 million, pension expense of $34,000 and other miscellaneous employee expenses of $75,000, offset in part by reductions in SERP expense of $0.2 million and ESOP expense of $16,000.&#160;&#160;In addition, occupancy and equipment expense increased $0.4 million primarily due to rental expenses and other miscellaneous expenses increased approximately $0.1 million, which is comprised of advertising and public relations, insurance and other expenses.&#160;&#160;Professional fees
decreased approximately $0.2 million due to reduced services and data processing fees decreased approximately $26,000.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Income Taxes.&#160;&#160;</font>Income tax expense increased $1.1 million, or 52.1%, to $3.3 million for fiscal year 2008, from $2.2 million for fiscal year 2007.&#160;&#160;This
increase was primarily due to increased income before taxes.&#160;&#160;The effective tax rate increased to 37.3% in fiscal year 2008, as compared to 36.2% in fiscal year 2007.</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Rate/Volume Analysis</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The following table presents the dollar amount of changes in interest income and interest expense for the major categories of our interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities. Information is provided for each category of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities with respect to (i) changes attributable to changes
in volume (<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">i.e</font>., changes in average balances multiplied by the prior-period average rate) and (ii) changes attributable to rate (<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">i.e</font>., changes in average rate multiplied by prior-period average balances).&#160;&#160;For purposes of this table, changes attributable to both rate and volume, which cannot be
segregated, have been allocated proportionately to the change due to volume and the change due to rate.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Liquidity and Capital Resources</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"></font><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We maintain liquid assets at levels we consider adequate to meet our liquidity needs.&#160;&#160;We adjust our liquidity levels to fund deposit outflows, pay real estate taxes on mortgage
loans, repay our borrowings and to fund loan commitments.&#160;&#160;We also adjust liquidity as appropriate to meet asset and liability management objectives.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"></font><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our primary sources of liquidity are deposits, amortization and prepayment of loans and mortgage-backed securities, maturities of investment securities and other short-term investments,
and earnings and funds provided from operations, as well as access to Federal Home Loan Bank advances.&#160;&#160;While scheduled principal repayments on loans and mortgage-backed securities are a relatively predictable source of funds, deposit flows and loan prepayments are greatly influenced by market interest rates, economic conditions and rates offered by our competition.&#160;&#160;We set the interest rates on our deposits to maintain a desired level of total deposits.&#160;&#160;In addition, we invest excess
funds in short-term interest-earning assets, which provide liquidity to meet lending requirements.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">

<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">&#160;</div></div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">51</font></div>
<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
<hr style="COLOR: gainsboro" noshade size="2"></div></div>
<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right">&#160;</div></div></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"></font><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">A significant portion of our liquidity consists of cash and cash equivalents, which are a product of our operating, investing and financing activities.&#160;&#160;At September 30, 2009,
$3.5&#160;million of our assets were invested in cash and due from banks.&#160;&#160;Our primary sources of cash are principal repayments on loans, proceeds from the calls and maturities of investment securities, principal repayments of mortgage-backed securities and increases in deposit accounts.&#160;&#160;Currently, we sell longer-term fixed rate mortgage loans, and we syndicate and sell participation interests in portions of our multi-family, commercial real estate and construction loans.&#160;&#160;This
activity may continue so long as it meets our operational and financial needs.&#160;&#160;In addition, we invest excess funds in short-term interest-earning assets and other assets, which provide liquidity to meet our lending requirements.&#160;&#160;There were no certificates of deposit and short-term investment securities (maturing in less than three years) at September 30, 2009.&#160;&#160;As of September 30, 2009, we had $27.3 million in borrowings outstanding from the Federal Home Loan Bank of New York and
we have access to additional Federal Home Loan Bank advances of up to $48.7&#160;million.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"></font><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At September 30, 2009, we had $121.4 million in loan commitments outstanding, which included $81.7 million in undisbursed construction loans, $0.4 million in one- to four-family loans,
$10.6 million in commercial real estate lines of credit, $4.0 million in unused home equity lines of credit, and $24.7 million to originate primarily multi-family and nonresidential mortgage loans.&#160;&#160;We also have one commercial letter of credit of $2.1 million.&#160;&#160;Certificates of deposit due within one year of September 30, 2009 totaled $190.8 million, or 76.1%, of certificates of deposit.&#160;&#160;The large percentage of certificates of deposits that mature within one year reflects customers&#8217;
hesitancy to invest their funds for long periods in the current low interest rate environment.&#160;&#160;If these maturing deposits do not remain with us, we will be required to seek other sources of funds, including other certificates of deposit and borrowings.&#160;&#160;Depending on market conditions, we may be required to pay higher rates on these deposits or other borrowings than we currently pay on the certificates of deposit due on or before September 30, 2010.&#160;&#160;We believe, however, based on
past experience that a significant portion of our certificates of deposit will remain with us.&#160;&#160;We have the ability to attract and retain deposits by adjusting the interest rates offered.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As reported in the consolidated statements of cash flows, our cash flows are classified by source for financial reporting purposes as operating, investing or financing cash flows.&#160;&#160;Net cash (used in) provided by operating activities was $(58.3) million and $(79.3)&#160;million and $26.7&#160;million for the years ended September
30, 2009, 2008, and 2007, respectively.&#160;&#160;These amounts differ from our net income because of a variety of cash receipts and disbursements that did not affect net income for the respective periods, the most significant of which are originations and sales of loans held-for-sale.&#160;&#160;The net effect of these originations and sales was a cash outflow of $78.1 million, a cash outflow of $110.7 million and a cash outflow of $10.6 million in fiscal years 2009, 2008, and 2007, respectively.&#160;&#160;Net
cash (used in) provided by investing activities was $17.0 million, $(6.2)&#160;million, and $1.1&#160;million in fiscal years 2009, 2008 and 2007, respectively, principally reflecting our loan and investment security activities in the respective periods.&#160;&#160;Investment securities net cash (purchases net of sales, principal repayments and maturities) provided by (used in), amounted to $3.5 million, $(4.9) million and $13.4 million in the years ended September 30, 2009, 2008 and 2007, respectively.&#160;&#160;In
fiscal year 2009, the cash flows generated from financing activities were utilized primarily for the repayment of borrowings after funding loan originations and investment security purchases.&#160;&#160;In fiscal year 2008, the cash flows generated from financing activities were utilized primarily for loan originations and investment security purchases.&#160;&#160;Net deposit inflow of $59.6 million, net repayments of Federal Home Loan Bank overnight and term advances of $16.9 million, purchase of treasury shares
of $1.3 million and payment of dividends of $1.5 million comprised most of our financing activities that resulted in net cash provided by financing activities of $39.7 million in fiscal year 2009, net proceeds of $34.9 million of Federal Home Loan Bank advances, purchase of treasury shares of $4.0 million and net deposit inflow of $55.3 million comprised most of our financing activities which resulted in net cash provided by financing activities of $85.1 million in fiscal year 2008 and net repayment of $40.1
million of Federal Home Loan Bank advances, purchase of treasury shares of $2.5 million and net deposit inflow of $16.2 million resulted in net cash used in of $26.6 million in fiscal year 2007.&#160;&#160;The net effect of our operating, investing and financing activities was to decrease our cash and cash equivalents from $4.1 million at the beginning of fiscal year 2007 to $3.5&#160;million at the end of fiscal year 2009.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"></font><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Off-Balance Sheet Arrangements.&#160;&#160;</font>In the normal course
of operations, we engage in a variety of financial transactions that, in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, are not recorded in our financial statements.&#160;&#160;These transactions involve, to varying degrees, elements of credit, interest rate and liquidity risk and are used primarily to manage customers&#8217; requests for funding and take the form of loan commitments and lines of credit.&#160;&#160;For information about our loan commitments and unused lines of credit, see note 15 of
the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right">&#160;</div></div></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"></font><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">For fiscal year 2009, we did not engage in any off-balance-sheet transactions other than loan origination and loan sale commitments in the normal course of our lending activities.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Impact of Inflation and Changing Prices</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"></font><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The consolidated financial statements and related notes have been prepared in accordance with United States generally accepted accounting principles (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;).&#160;&#160;GAAP
generally requires the measurement of financial position and operating results in terms of historical dollars without consideration for changes in the relative purchasing power of money over time due to inflation.&#160;&#160;The impact of inflation is reflected in the increased cost of our operations.&#160;&#160;Unlike industrial companies, our assets and liabilities are primarily monetary in nature.&#160;&#160;As a result, changes in market interest rates have a greater impact on performance than do the effects
of inflation.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Item 7A.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"></font><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">General</font>.&#160;&#160;The majority of our assets and liabilities
are monetary in nature.&#160;&#160;Consequently, our most significant form of market risk is interest rate risk.&#160;&#160;Our assets, consisting primarily of mortgage loans, have longer maturities than our liabilities, consisting primarily of deposits.&#160;&#160;As a result, a principal part of our business strategy is to manage interest rate risk and reduce the exposure of our net interest income to changes in market interest rates.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, our board of directors has approved guidelines for
managing the interest rate risk inherent in our assets and liabilities, given our business strategy, operating environment, capital, liquidity and performance objectives.&#160;&#160;Senior management monitors the level of interest rate risk on a regular basis and the audit committee of the board of directors meets as needed to review our asset/liability policies and interest rate risk position.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"></font><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We have sought to manage our interest rate risk in order to minimize the exposure of our earnings and capital to changes in interest rates.&#160;&#160;During the low interest rate environment
that has existed in recent years, we have implemented the following strategies to manage our interest rate risk:&#160;&#160;(i) maintaining a high level of short-term liquid assets invested in cash and cash equivalents, short-term securities and mortgage-related securities that provide significant cash flows; (ii)&#160;generally selling longer-term mortgage loans; and (iii) lengthening the average term of our certificates of deposit.&#160;&#160;By investing in short-term, liquid instruments, we believe we are
better positioned to react to increases in market interest rates.&#160;&#160;However, investments in shorter-term securities and cash and cash equivalents generally bear lower yields than longer-term investments.&#160;&#160;Thus, during periods of declining interest rates, our strategy of investing in liquid instruments has resulted in lower levels of interest income than would have resulted from investing in longer-term loans and investments.&#160;&#160;The net proceeds from the offering have increased our capital
and provided management with greater flexibility to manage our interest rate risk.&#160;&#160;In particular, management has leveraged the capital we received to increase our interest-earning assets.&#160;&#160;Management intends to lengthen the maturity of our earning assets as interest rates increase, which, in turn, should result in a higher yielding portfolio of interest-earning assets.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Net Portfolio Value.</font>&#160;&#160;The Office of Thrift Supervision requires the computation of amounts by which the net present value of an institution&#8217;s
cash flow from assets, liabilities and off-balance sheet items (the institution&#8217;s net portfolio value or &#8220;NPV&#8221;) would change in the event of a range of assumed changes in market interest rates.&#160;&#160;The Office of Thrift Supervision provides all institutions that file a Consolidated Maturity/Rate Schedule as a part of their quarterly Thrift Financial Report with an interest rate sensitivity report of net portfolio value.&#160;&#160;The Office of Thrift Supervision simulation model uses
a discounted cash flow analysis and an option-based pricing approach to measuring the interest rate sensitivity of net portfolio value.&#160;&#160;Historically, the Office of Thrift Supervision model estimated the economic value of each type of asset, liability and off-balance sheet contract under the assumption that the United States Treasury yield curve increases or decreases instantaneously by 100 to 300 basis points in 100 basis point increments.&#160;&#160;A basis point equals one-hundredth of one percent,
and 100 basis points equals one percent.&#160;&#160;An increase in interest rates from 3% to 4% would mean, for example, a 100 basis point increase in the &#8220;Change in Interest Rates&#8221; column below.&#160;&#160;The Office of Thrift Supervision provides us the results of the interest rate sensitivity model, which is based on information we provide to the Office of Thrift Supervision to estimate the sensitivity of our net portfolio value.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: left">&#160;</div>

<div align="left">
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td align="right" width="4%" style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(1)&#160;&#160;</font></div></td>
<td width="96%">
<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">Assumes an instantaneous uniform change in interest rates at all maturities.</font></div></td></tr></table></div>
<div align="left">
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td align="right" width="4%" style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(2)&#160;&#160;</font></div></td>
<td width="96%">
<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">NPV is the discounted present value of expected cash flows from assets, liabilities and off-balance sheet contracts.</font></div></td></tr></table></div>
<div align="left">
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td align="right" width="4%" style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(3)&#160;&#160;</font></div></td>
<td width="96%">
<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">Present value of assets represents the discounted present value of incoming cash flows on interest-earning assets.</font></div></td></tr></table></div>
<div align="left">
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td align="right" width="4%" style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(4)&#160;&#160;</font></div></td>
<td width="96%">
<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">NPV Ratio represents NPV divided by the present value of assets.</font></div></td></tr></table></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"></font><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The table above indicates that at September 30, 2009, in the event of a 100 basis point decrease in interest rates, we would experience a 2% decrease in net portfolio value.&#160;&#160;In
the event of a 200 basis point increase in interest rates, we would experience a 1% decrease in net portfolio value.&#160;&#160;Our interest rate risk management policy in the low interest rate environment that has existed in recent years has emphasized maintaining a significant percentage of our assets in cash and cash equivalents, shorter-term securities and mortgage-related securities that provide significant cash flows.&#160;&#160;The effect of this policy has been to reduce our level of net interest income.&#160;&#160;We
have been willing to accept reduced levels of income in low interest rate environments in order to be better positioned to reinvest our assets in longer-term, higher yielding investments as interest rates rise.</font></font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"></font><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Certain shortcomings are inherent in the methodology used in the above interest rate risk measurement.&#160;&#160;Modeling changes in net portfolio value requires making certain assumptions
that may or may not reflect the manner in which actual yields and costs respond to changes in market interest rates.&#160;&#160;In this regard, the net portfolio value table presented assumes that the composition of our interest-sensitive assets and liabilities existing at the beginning of a period remains constant over the period being measured and assumes that a particular change in interest rates is reflected uniformly across the yield curve regardless of the duration or repricing of specific assets and liabilities.&#160;&#160;Accordingly,
although the net portfolio value table provides an indication of our interest rate risk exposure at a particular point in time, it is not intended to and does not provide a precise forecast of the effect of changes in market interest rates on our net interest income and will differ from actual results.</font></font></div>

<br></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States).&#160;&#160;Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the consolidated financial statements are free of material
misstatement.&#160;&#160;The Company is not required to have, nor were we engaged to perform, an audit of its internal control over financial reporting.&#160;&#160;Our audit included consideration of internal control over financial reporting as a basis for designing audit procedures that are appropriate in the circumstances, but not for the purpose of expressing an opinion on the effectiveness of the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, we express no such opinion.&#160;&#160;An
audit also includes examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the consolidated financial statements, assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall consolidated financial statement presentation.&#160;&#160;We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div>

<div align="left">

<td width="5%" style="WIDTH: 36pt; TEXT-ALIGN: left">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(1)&#160;&#160;</font></div></td>
<td width="95%">
<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160;Reorganization and Stock Offering</font></div></td></tr></table></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On April 5, 2005, Brooklyn Federal Savings Bank (the &#8220;Bank&#8221;) completed its reorganization into a mutual holding company structure (the &#8220;Reorganization&#8221;).&#160;&#160;As part of the Reorganization, the Bank converted from a federally-chartered mutual savings bank to a federally-chartered stock savings bank (the &#8220;Conversion&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The
Bank became the wholly-owned subsidiary of Brooklyn Federal Bancorp, Inc., a federal corporation (the &#8220;Company&#8221;), which became the majority-owned subsidiary of Brooklyn Bancorp, MHC (the &#8220;Mutual Holding Company&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The Company issued a total of 13,225,000 common shares on April 5, 2005, consisting of 3,967,500 shares (30%) sold to the public (the &#8220;Offering&#8221;) and 9,257,500 shares (70%) issued to the Mutual Holding Company.&#160;&#160;The gross proceeds from the offering
were approximately $39.7 million, less offering costs of approximately $1.8 million.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div align="left">
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td width="5%" style="WIDTH: 36pt; TEXT-ALIGN: left">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">(2)&#160;&#160;</font></div></td>
<td width="95%">
<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160;Nature of Business and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</font></font></div></td></tr></table></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Bank is a community-oriented savings institution whose business primarily consists of accepting deposits from customers within its market area (Brooklyn, Nassau and Suffolk Counties, New York) and investing those funds principally in mortgage loans secured by one- to four-family residences, multi-family properties and commercial properties,
and in mortgage-backed securities.&#160;&#160;Substantially all of the Bank&#8217;s loans are collateralized or dependent on real estate.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Effective July&#160;1, 2009, we adopted the provisions of Financial Accounting Standards Board, or FASB, Accounting Standards Codification&#8482;, (the &#8220;FASB ASC&#8221;), which is now the source of authoritative, non-governmental U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;). While the FASB ASC did not change
GAAP, all existing authoritative accounting literature, with certain exceptions, was superseded and codified into the FASB ASC. The references to authoritative accounting literature contained in our disclosures have been modified to refer to general accounting topics within the FASB ASC.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Deposits are insured up to applicable limits by the Deposit Insurance Fund of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (&#8220;FDIC&#8221;). The Bank&#8217;s and the Company&#8217;s primary regulator is the Office of Thrift Supervision (&#8220;OTS&#8221;).</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div align="left">
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">

<td align="right" width="5%" style="WIDTH: 49px">

<td width="5%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;(a)&#160;</font></font></td>
<td width="90%">
<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160; Basis of</font> <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">Presentation</font></font></font></div></td></tr></table></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 72pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The accompanying consolidated financial statements are prepared in conformity with&#160;&#160;GAAP and include the accounts of the Company, the Bank and the Bank&#8217;s wholly owned subsidiaries (collectively, the &#8220;Company&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The Bank&#8217;s wholly-owned subsidiaries are Thrift Investors Service Corporation (&#8220;TISCO&#8221;),
3D Holding Corp., Inc., and BFS REIT, Inc. (&#8220;BFS REIT&#8221;).&#160;&#160;BFS REIT is a real estate investment trust formed to hold mortgage-related assets. TISCO&#8217;s wholly owned subsidiary, BFS Agency, provides insurance services to the customers of the Bank. 3D Holding Corp., Inc., was formed to hold title to certain properties acquired by the Bank through foreclosure. All significant inter-company balances and transactions are eliminated in consolidation.</font></div>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: left">&#160;</div>
<div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
